bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 卷第一百九

translations.literal: Volume 109
translations.idiomatic: Volume 109

sentences.zh: 【晉紀三十一】強圉作噩，一年

translations.literal: [Jin Records, Thirty-One] Qiangyu Zuo'e, one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records, Part 31] The year Qiangyu Zuo'e—one year in all.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝甲隆安元年

translations.literal: Emperor An's jia, first year of Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: The first year of the Long'an era of Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥朔，帝加元服，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jihai new moon, the Emperor assumed the cap of manhood and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the jihai new moon, Emperor An assumed the cap of manhood and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 以左僕射王珣為尚書令；

translations.literal: Wang Xun, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍王國寶為左僕射，領選，仍加後將軍、丹楊尹。

translations.literal: General of the Household Guards Wang Guobao was made Left Vice Director, with charge of selection; he was also given the additional titles of General of the Rear and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Household Guards Wang Guobao was made Left Vice Director with charge of selection; he was also given the additional titles of General of the Rear and Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子悉以東宮兵配國寶，使領之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi, transferred all Eastern Palace troops to Guobao for him to command.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Daozi, transferred all Eastern Palace troops to Guobao for him to command.

sentences.zh: 燕范陽王德求救於秦，秦兵不出。

translations.literal: Later Yan's Prince of Fanyang, De, asked Qin for rescue; Qin troops did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan's Prince of Fanyang, Murong De, asked Former Qin for rescue, but Qin troops did not march out.

sentences.zh: 鄴中恟懼。

translations.literal: Within Ye there was alarm and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Within Ye there was alarm and fear.

sentences.zh: 賀賴盧自以魏王珪之舅，不受東平公儀節度，由是與儀有隙。

translations.literal: Helai Lu, considering himself the maternal uncle of Northern Wei's King Gui, refused to accept the command of the Duke of Dongping, Yi; because of this he had a rift with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Helai Lu, considering himself the maternal uncle of Northern Wei's King Tuoba Gui, refused to accept orders from the Duke of Dongping, Murong Yi, and thereby fell out with Yi.

sentences.zh: 儀司馬丁建陰與德通，從而構間之，射書入城中言其狀。

translations.literal: Yi's marshal Ding Jian secretly communicated with De and sowed discord between them, shooting a letter into the city stating the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's marshal Ding Jian secretly communicated with De and sowed discord between them, shooting a letter into the city that laid out the situation.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，風霾，晝晦。

translations.literal: On jiachen, wind and dust darkened the sky; day was dim.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, wind and dust darkened the sky until broad daylight turned dim.

sentences.zh: 賴盧營有火，建言於儀曰：「賴盧燒營為變矣。」

translations.literal: There was fire in Helai Lu's camp; he said to Yi, "Helai Lu has burned his camp to stage a mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: There was fire in Helai Lu's camp; he told Yi, "Helai Lu has burned his camp to stage a mutiny."

sentences.zh: 儀以為然，引兵退。

translations.literal: Yi believed it and withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yi believed it and withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 賴盧聞之，亦退。

translations.literal: When Helai Lu heard of it, he too withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Helai Lu heard of it, he too withdrew.

sentences.zh: 建帥其眾詣德降，且言儀師老可擊。

translations.literal: Jian led his followers to surrender to De, and also said that Yi's army was worn out and could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Jian led his followers to surrender to De, and also said that Yi's army was worn out and could be attacked.

sentences.zh: 德遣桂陽王鎮、南安王青帥騎七千追擊魏軍，大破之。

translations.literal: De sent the Prince of Guiyang, Zhen, and the Prince of Nan'an, Qing, to lead seven thousand horsemen in pursuit of the Wei army and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: De sent the Prince of Guiyang, Murong Zhen, and the Prince of Nan'an, Murong Qing, to lead seven thousand horsemen in pursuit of the Wei army and inflicted a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶使左衛將軍慕輿騰攻博陵，殺魏所置守宰。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Bao sent the Left Guard General Murong Teng to attack Boling and killed the magistrates Wei had installed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan ruler Murong Bao sent the Left Guard General Murong Teng to attack Boling and killed the magistrates Wei had installed.

sentences.zh: 王建等攻信都，六十餘日不下，士卒多死。

translations.literal: Wang Jian and others besieged Xindu for more than sixty days without taking it; many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian and others besieged Xindu for more than sixty days without taking it, and many soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 庚申，魏王珪自攻信都。

translations.literal: On gengshen, King Gui of Wei personally attacked Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, King Tuoba Gui of Wei personally attacked Xindu.

sentences.zh: 壬戌夜，燕宜都王鳳逾城奔中山。

translations.literal: On the night of renxu, Yan's Prince of Yidu, Feng, climbed over the wall and fled to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of renxu, Yan's Prince of Yidu, Murong Feng, climbed over the wall and fled to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，信都降魏。

translations.literal: On guihai, Xindu surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Xindu surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 涼王光以西秦王乾歸數反覆，舉兵伐之。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler Guang, because the Western Qin ruler Qian'gui had repeatedly turned back on him, raised troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang ruler Lü Guang, because the Western Qin ruler Qifu Qian'gui had repeatedly turned back on him, raised troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 乾歸群下請東奔成紀以避之，乾歸曰：「軍之勝敗，在於巧拙，不在眾寡。

translations.literal: Qian'gui's subordinates asked to flee east to Chengjji to avoid him; Qian'gui said, "Victory or defeat in war lies in skill and cunning, not in numbers alone.
translations.idiomatic: Qian'gui's subordinates asked to flee east to Chengjji to avoid him; Qian'gui said, "Victory or defeat in war lies in skill and cunning, not in numbers alone.

sentences.zh: 光兵雖眾而無法，其弟延勇而無謀，不足憚也。

translations.literal: Guang's army is numerous but without discipline; his brother Yan is brave but without strategy—there is nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's army is numerous but without discipline; his brother Yan is brave but without strategy—there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 且其精兵盡在延所，延敗，光自走矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, his crack troops are all with Yan; if Yan is defeated, Guang will flee on his own."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his crack troops are all with Yan; if Yan is defeated, Guang will flee on his own."

sentences.zh: 光軍於長最，遣太原公纂等帥步騎三萬攻金城；

translations.literal: Guang's army was at Changzui; he sent the Prince of Taiyuan, Zuan, and others to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Jincheng;
translations.idiomatic: Guang's army was at Changzui; he sent the Prince of Taiyuan, Lü Zuan, and others to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Jincheng;

sentences.zh: 乾歸帥眾二萬救之，未到，纂等拔金城。

translations.literal: Qian'gui led twenty thousand men to rescue it; before he arrived, Zuan and the others had already taken Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian'gui led twenty thousand men to rescue it; before he arrived, Zuan and the others had already taken Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 光又遣其將梁恭等以甲卒萬餘出陽武下峽，與秦州刺史沒弈干攻其東，天水公延以枹罕之眾攻臨洮、武始、河關，皆克之。

translations.literal: Guang also sent his generals Liang Gong and others with more than ten thousand armored soldiers out through Yangwu down the gorge, to join the Qinzhou inspector Moyigan in attacking Qian'gui's east; the Duke of Tianshui, Yan, with the troops of Fuhan attacked Lintao, Wushi, and Heguan, and all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also sent his generals Liang Gong and others with more than ten thousand armored soldiers out through Yangwu down the gorge, to join the Qinzhou inspector Moyigan in attacking Qian'gui's east; the Duke of Tianshui, Lü Yan, with the troops of Fuhan attacked Lintao, Wushi, and Heguan, and all were taken.

sentences.zh: 乾歸使人紿延云：「乾歸眾潰，奔成紀。」

translations.literal: Qian'gui had someone deceive Yan, saying, "Qian'gui's host has scattered and fled to Chengjji."
translations.idiomatic: Qian'gui had someone deceive Yan, saying, "Qian'gui's host has scattered and fled to Chengjji."

sentences.zh: 延欲引以輕騎追之，司馬耿稚諫曰：「乾歸勇略過人，安肯望風自潰？

translations.literal: Yan wished to lead light cavalry in pursuit; the marshal Geng Zhi remonstrated, "Qian'gui's courage and stratagem surpass other men—how could he flee at the mere rumor of wind?
translations.idiomatic: Yan wished to lead light cavalry in pursuit; the marshal Geng Zhi remonstrated, "Qian'gui's courage and stratagem surpass other men—how could he flee at the mere rumor of wind?

sentences.zh: 前破王廣、楊定，皆羸師以誘之。

translations.literal: In defeating Wang Guang and Yang Ding before, he used weakened troops to lure them in.
translations.idiomatic: In defeating Wang Guang and Yang Ding before, he used weakened troops to lure them in.

sentences.zh: 今告者視高色動，殆必有奸，宜整陳而前，使步騎相屬，俟諸軍畢集，然後擊之，無不克矣。」

translations.literal: The messenger now looks up and his color shifts—there is probably treachery; you should advance in battle order with infantry and cavalry linked, wait until all armies are assembled, and then strike—nothing will fail to be taken."
translations.idiomatic: The messenger now looks up and his color shifts—there is probably treachery; you should advance in battle order with infantry and cavalry linked, wait until all armies are assembled, and then strike—nothing will fail to be taken."

sentences.zh: 延不從，進，與乾歸遇，延戰死。

translations.literal: Yan did not listen, advanced, met Qian'gui, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yan did not listen, advanced, met Qian'gui, and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 稚與將軍姜顯牧散卒，還屯枹罕。

translations.literal: Zhi and the general Jiang Xianmu gathered the scattered troops and returned to camp at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and the general Jiang Xianmu gathered the scattered troops and returned to camp at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 光亦引兵還姑臧。

translations.literal: Guang also led his army back to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also led his army back to Guzang.

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、西平王，大赦，改元太初。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu declared himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Xiping; he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu declared himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Xiping; he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Taichu.

sentences.zh: 治兵廣武，攻涼金城，克之。

translations.literal: He drilled troops at Guangwu and attacked Later Liang's Jincheng, taking it.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled troops at Guangwu and attacked Later Liang's Jincheng, taking it.

sentences.zh: 涼王光遣將軍竇苟伐之，戰於街亭，涼兵大敗。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler Guang sent the general Dou Gou to attack him; they fought at Jieting, and the Liang army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang ruler Lü Guang sent the general Dou Gou to attack him; they fought at Jieting, and the Liang army suffered a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶聞魏王珪攻信都，出屯深澤，遣趙王麟攻楊城，殺守兵三百。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Bao, hearing that King Gui of Wei was attacking Xindu, went out to camp at Shenze and sent the Prince of Zhao, Lin, to attack Yangcheng, killing three hundred garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan ruler Murong Bao, hearing that King Tuoba Gui of Wei was attacking Xindu, went out to camp at Shenze and sent the Prince of Zhao, Murong Lin, to attack Yangcheng, killing three hundred garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 寶悉出珍寶及宮人募郡縣君盜以擊魏。

translations.literal: Bao brought out all treasures and palace women to recruit county and district bravado to strike Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bao brought out all treasures and palace women to recruit county and district bravado to strike Wei.

sentences.zh: 二月，己巳朔，珪還屯楊城。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the yisi new moon, Gui returned to camp at Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the yisi new moon, Tuoba Gui returned to camp at Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 沒根兄子丑提為并州監軍，聞其叔父降燕，懼誅，帥所部兵還國作亂。

translations.literal: Chouti, nephew of Moyigen's elder brother, was supervising Bingzhou; hearing that his uncle had surrendered to Yan, he feared execution and led his troops back home in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Chouti, nephew of Moyigan's elder brother, was supervising Bingzhou; hearing that his uncle had surrendered to Yan, he feared execution and led his troops back home in revolt.

sentences.zh: 珪欲北還，遣其國相涉延求和於燕，且請以其弟為質。

translations.literal: Gui wished to return north and sent his chief minister Sheyan to seek peace with Yan, and also asked to give his younger brother as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Gui wished to return north and sent his chief minister Sheyan to seek peace with Yan, and also asked to give his younger brother as hostage.

sentences.zh: 寶聞魏有內難，不許，使冗從僕射蘭真責珪負恩，悉發其眾步卒十二萬、騎三萬七千屯於曲陽之柏肆，營於滹沲水北以邀之。

translations.literal: Bao, hearing that Wei had internal troubles, did not agree; he sent the attendant-at-court Lan Zhen to reproach Gui for ingratitude, and mustered his entire host—one hundred twenty thousand foot soldiers and thirty-seven thousand horsemen—to camp at Baixi in Quyang, encamping north of the Hutuo River to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, hearing that Wei had internal troubles, did not agree; he sent the attendant-at-court Lan Zhen to reproach Gui for ingratitude, and mustered his entire host—one hundred twenty thousand foot soldiers and thirty-seven thousand horsemen—to camp at Baixi in Quyang, encamping north of the Hutuo River to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，魏軍至，營於水南。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the Wei army arrived and encamped south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, the Wei army arrived and encamped south of the river.

sentences.zh: 寶潛師夜濟，募勇敢萬餘人襲魏營，寶陳於營北以為之援。

translations.literal: Bao secretly sent troops across the river by night, recruited more than ten thousand brave men to raid the Wei camp, and Bao drew up his battle line north of the camp to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao secretly sent troops across the river by night, recruited more than ten thousand brave men to raid the Wei camp, and Bao drew up his battle line north of the camp to support them.

sentences.zh: 募兵因風縱火。

translations.literal: The recruited soldiers took advantage of the wind to set fires.
translations.idiomatic: The recruited soldiers took advantage of the wind to set fires.

sentences.zh: 急擊魏軍，魏軍大亂，珪驚起，棄營跣走；

translations.literal: They pressed the attack on the Wei army; the Wei army fell into great disorder; Gui started up in alarm, abandoned camp, and fled barefoot;
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack on the Wei army; the Wei army fell into great disorder; Gui started up in alarm, abandoned camp, and fled barefoot;

sentences.zh: 燕將軍乞特真帥百餘人至其帳下，得珪衣靴。

translations.literal: The Yan general Qi Tezhen led more than a hundred men to his tent and obtained Gui's clothes and boots.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan general Qi Tezhen led more than a hundred men to his tent and obtained Gui's clothes and boots.

sentences.zh: 既而募兵無故自驚，互相斫射。

translations.literal: Presently the recruited soldiers panicked for no reason and hacked and shot at one another.
translations.idiomatic: Presently the recruited soldiers panicked for no reason and hacked and shot at one another.

sentences.zh: 珪於營外望見之，乃擊鼓收眾，左右及中軍將士舟稍稍來集，多布火炬於營外，縱騎沖之。

translations.literal: Gui, watching from outside the camp, beat the drum to gather his men; guards and central-army officers gradually came together; he set many torches outside the camp and sent horsemen to charge them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, watching from outside the camp, beat the drum to gather his men; guards and central-army officers gradually came together; he set many torches outside the camp and sent horsemen to charge them.

sentences.zh: 募兵大敗，還赴寶陳，寶引兵復渡水北。

translations.literal: The recruited soldiers were utterly defeated; they returned to Bao's battle line, and Bao led his army back across the river to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The recruited soldiers were utterly defeated; they returned to Bao's battle line, and Bao led his army back across the river to the north.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，魏整眾而至，與燕相持，燕軍奪氣。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Wei army reformed and arrived; the two sides faced off, and the Yan army lost its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the Wei army reformed and arrived; the two sides faced off, and the Yan army lost its spirit.

sentences.zh: 寶引還中山，魏兵隨而擊之，燕兵屢敗。

translations.literal: Bao withdrew to Zhongshan; the Wei army pursued and struck; the Yan army was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bao withdrew to Zhongshan; the Wei army pursued and struck; the Yan army was repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 寶懼，棄大軍，帥騎二萬奔還。

translations.literal: Bao was afraid, abandoned the main army, and led twenty thousand horsemen in flight back.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was afraid, abandoned the main army, and led twenty thousand horsemen in flight back.

sentences.zh: 時大風雪，凍死者相枕。

translations.literal: At that time a great wind and snow blew; the dead from freezing lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a great wind and snow blew; the dead from freezing lay pillow to pillow.

sentences.zh: 寶恐為魏軍所及，命士卒皆棄袍仗、兵器數十萬，寸刃不返，燕之朝臣將卒降魏及為魏所繫虜者甚眾。

translations.literal: Bao, fearing the Wei army would overtake him, ordered his soldiers to abandon robes, gear, and weapons by the hundreds of thousands—not a blade returned—and many Yan courtiers, generals, and soldiers surrendered to Wei or were captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, fearing the Wei army would overtake him, ordered his soldiers to abandon robes, gear, and weapons by the hundreds of thousands—not a blade returned—and many Yan courtiers, generals, and soldiers surrendered to Wei or were captured by Wei.

sentences.zh: 先是，張袞常為魏王珪言燕秘書監崔逞之材，珪得之，甚喜，以逞為尚書，使錄三十六曹，任以政事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Gun had often told King Gui of Wei of the talent of Yan's Secretariat Director Cui Cheng; Gui obtained him, was greatly pleased, made Cheng Director of the Imperial Secretariat, had him oversee the thirty-six bureaus, and entrusted him with government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Gun had often told King Tuoba Gui of Wei of the talent of Yan's Secretariat Director Cui Cheng; Gui obtained him, was greatly pleased, made Cheng Director of the Imperial Secretariat, had him oversee the thirty-six bureaus, and entrusted him with government affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏軍士有自柏肆亡歸者，言大軍敗散，不知王處。

translations.literal: Among the Wei soldiers were some who had fled from Baixi and returned, saying the main army was defeated and scattered and they did not know where the king was.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Wei soldiers were some who had fled from Baixi and returned, saying the main army was defeated and scattered and they did not know where the king was.

sentences.zh: 道過晉陽，晉陽守將封真因起兵攻并州刺史曲陽侯素延，素延擊斬之。

translations.literal: Passing Jinyang, the Jinyang garrison commander Feng Zhen thereupon raised troops to attack the Bingzhou inspector, the Marquis of Quyang, Su Yan; Su Yan struck and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Jinyang, the Jinyang garrison commander Feng Zhen thereupon raised troops to attack the Bingzhou inspector, the Marquis of Quyang, Su Yan; Su Yan struck and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 南安公順守雲中，聞之，欲自攝國事。

translations.literal: The Duke of Nan'an, Shun, was holding Yunzhong; when he heard of it, he wished to take charge of state affairs himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Nan'an, Tuoba Shun, was holding Yunzhong; when he heard of it, he wished to take charge of state affairs himself.

sentences.zh: 幢將代人莫題曰：「此大事，不可輕爾，宜審待後問；

translations.literal: The standard-bearer Mo Ti of the Xianbei said, "This is a great matter and cannot be taken lightly; you should wait carefully for further word;
translations.idiomatic: The standard-bearer Mo Ti of the Xianbei said, "This is a great matter and cannot be taken lightly; you should wait carefully for further word;

sentences.zh: 不然，為禍不細。」

translations.literal: otherwise the harm will be no small thing."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the harm will be no small thing."

sentences.zh: 順乃止。

translations.literal: Shun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shun then stopped.

sentences.zh: 順，什翼犍之孫也。

translations.literal: Shun was the grandson of Shiyijian.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was the grandson of Tuoba Shiyijian.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭部帥附力眷、紇鄰部帥匿物尼、紇奚部帥叱奴根皆舉兵反，順討之，不克。

translations.literal: The Helan chieftain Fuli Juan, the Heni chieftain Niwuni, and the Hexi chieftain Chinu Gen all raised troops in revolt; Shun campaigned against them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The Helan chieftain Fuli Juan, the Heni chieftain Niwuni, and the Hexi chieftain Chinu Gen all raised troops in revolt; Shun campaigned against them but could not overcome them.

sentences.zh: 珪遣安遠將軍庾岳帥萬騎還討三部，皆平之，國人乃安。

translations.literal: Gui sent the General Who Pacifies the Distance Yu Yue to lead ten thousand horsemen back to suppress the three tribes; all were pacified, and the realm was then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gui sent the General Who Pacifies the Distance Yu Yue to lead ten thousand horsemen back to suppress the three tribes; all were pacified, and the realm was then at peace.

sentences.zh: 珪欲撫尉新附，深悔參合之誅，素延坐討反者殺戮過多，免官；

translations.literal: Gui wished to comfort and reassure the newly submitted; he deeply regretted the slaughter at Canhe; Su Yan was removed from office for killing too many in suppressing rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Gui wished to comfort and reassure the newly submitted; he deeply regretted the slaughter at Canhe; Su Yan was removed from office for killing too many in suppressing rebels;

sentences.zh: 以奚牧為并州刺史。

translations.literal: Xi Mu was made inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Mu was made inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 牧與東秦主興書稱「頓首」，與之均禮。

translations.literal: Mu wrote to the Eastern Qin ruler Xing with the salutation "bowing head," treating him as an equal in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Mu wrote to the Eastern Qin ruler Yao Xing with the salutation "bowing head," treating him as an equal in ritual.

sentences.zh: 興怒，以告珪，珪為之殺牧。

translations.literal: Xing was angry and reported it to Gui; Gui had Mu killed for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was angry and reported it to Gui; Gui had Mu killed for it.

sentences.zh: 己卯夜，燕尚書郎慕輿謀弒燕主寶，立趙王麟；

translations.literal: On the night of jimao, Yan's Master of Writing Murong Mou attempted to assassinate the Yan ruler Bao and install the Prince of Zhao, Lin;
translations.idiomatic: On the night of jimao, Yan's Master of Writing Murong Mou attempted to assassinate the Yan ruler Murong Bao and install the Prince of Zhao, Murong Lin;

sentences.zh: 不克，斬關出奔魏。

translations.literal: he did not succeed, broke through the gate, and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: he did not succeed, broke through the gate, and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 麟由是不自安。

translations.literal: Lin was thereby ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was thereby ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 三月，燕以儀同三司武鄉張崇為司空。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yan appointed Zhang Chong of Wuxiang, with the rank equal to the Three Excellencies, as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Yan appointed Zhang Chong of Wuxiang, with the rank equal to the Three Excellencies, as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，燕清河王會聞魏軍東下，表求赴難，燕主寶許之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yan's Prince of Qinghe, Hui, hearing that the Wei army was marching east, memorialized asking to go to the rescue; the Yan ruler Bao permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yan's Prince of Qinghe, Murong Hui, hearing that the Wei army was marching east, memorialized asking to go to the rescue; the Yan ruler Murong Bao permitted it.

sentences.zh: 會初無去意，使征南將軍庫辱官偉、建威將軍餘崇將兵五千為前鋒。

translations.literal: Hui at first had no intention of leaving; he sent the General Who Conquers the South Kuluo Guan Wei and the General Who Establishes Prestige Yu Chong to lead five thousand men as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Hui at first had no intention of leaving; he sent the General Who Conquers the South Kuluo Guan Wei and the General Who Establishes Prestige Yu Chong to lead five thousand men as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 崇，嵩之子也。

translations.literal: Chong was the son of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was the son of Yu Song.

sentences.zh: 偉等頓盧龍近百日，無食，啖馬牛且盡，會不發。

translations.literal: Wei and the others halted at Lulong for nearly a hundred days without food, eating horses and cattle until they were nearly gone, yet Hui did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and the others halted at Lulong for nearly a hundred days without food, eating horses and cattle until they were nearly gone, yet Hui did not set out.

sentences.zh: 寶怒，累詔切責；

translations.literal: Bao was angry and repeatedly issued edicts sternly reproaching him;
translations.idiomatic: Bao was angry and repeatedly issued edicts sternly reproaching him;

sentences.zh: 會不得已，以治行簡練為名，復留月餘。

translations.literal: Hui had no choice; famed for his frugal and efficient administration, he lingered yet another month.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had no choice; famed for his frugal and efficient administration, he lingered yet another month.

sentences.zh: 時道路不通，偉欲使輕軍前行通道，偵魏強弱，且張聲勢；

translations.literal: At that time the roads were impassable; Wei wished to send light troops ahead to open the route, scout Wei's strength, and also make a show of force;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the roads were impassable; Wei wished to send light troops ahead to open the route, scout Wei's strength, and also make a show of force;

sentences.zh: 諸將皆畏避不欲行。

translations.literal: the generals all shrank back in fear and did not wish to go.
translations.idiomatic: the generals all shrank back in fear and did not wish to go.

sentences.zh: 餘崇奮曰：「今巨寇滔天，京都危逼，匹夫猶思致命以救君父，諸君荷國寵任，而更惜生乎！

translations.literal: Yu Chong roused himself and said, "Now the great enemy fills the heavens, and the capital is in peril; even a common man thinks of giving his life to save his ruler and father—yet you, bearing the state's favor and charge, still cling to life!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chong roused himself and said, "Now the great enemy fills the heavens, and the capital is in peril; even a common man thinks of giving his life to save his ruler and father—yet you, bearing the state's favor and charge, still cling to life!

sentences.zh: 若社稷傾覆，臣節不立，死有餘辱。

translations.literal: If the altars of state are overturned and ministerial integrity is not upheld, death itself still leaves shame.
translations.idiomatic: If the altars of state are overturned and ministerial integrity is not upheld, death itself still leaves shame.

sentences.zh: 諸君安居於此，崇請當之。」

translations.literal: You all may rest easy here—I ask to go myself."
translations.idiomatic: You all may rest easy here—I ask to go myself."

sentences.zh: 偉喜，簡給步騎五百人。

translations.literal: Wei was pleased and selected five hundred infantry and cavalry to give him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was pleased and selected five hundred infantry and cavalry to give him.

sentences.zh: 崇進至漁陽，遇魏千餘騎，崇謂其眾曰：「彼眾我寡，不擊則不得免。」

translations.literal: Chong advanced to Fuyang and encountered more than a thousand Wei horsemen; Chong told his men, "They are many and we are few; if we do not strike we cannot escape."
translations.idiomatic: Chong advanced to Fuyang and encountered more than a thousand Wei horsemen; Chong told his men, "They are many and we are few; if we do not strike we cannot escape."

sentences.zh: 乃鼓噪直進，崇手殺十餘人。

translations.literal: He then beat drums and shouted and charged straight ahead; Chong himself killed more than ten men.
translations.idiomatic: He then beat drums and shouted and charged straight ahead; Chong himself killed more than ten men.

sentences.zh: 魏騎潰去，崇亦引還，斬首獲生，具言敵中闊狹，眾心稍振。

translations.literal: The Wei horsemen broke and fled; Chong also withdrew, taking heads and captives, and fully reported the enemy's numbers and dispositions; the men's hearts were somewhat revived.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei horsemen broke and fled; Chong also withdrew, taking heads and captives, and fully reported the enemy's numbers and dispositions; the men's hearts were somewhat revived.

sentences.zh: 會乃上道徐進，是月，始達薊城。

translations.literal: Hui then took the road and advanced slowly; that month he finally reached Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then took the road and advanced slowly; that month he finally reached Ji.

sentences.zh: 魏圍中山既久，城中將士皆思出戰。

translations.literal: Wei had besieged Zhongshan for a long time; within the city generals and soldiers all wished to sally out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had besieged Zhongshan for a long time; within the city generals and soldiers all wished to sally out and fight.

sentences.zh: 征北大將軍隆言於寶曰：「涉珪雖屢獲小利，然頓兵經年，凶勢沮屈，士馬死傷太半，人心思歸，諸部離散，正是可破之時也。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the North Long said to Bao, "Though Shegui has repeatedly gained small advantages, he has halted his army for a year; his fierce momentum is broken and bent, horses and men dead and wounded beyond half, men's hearts think of return, the various tribes are scattered—this is precisely the time he can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: The General Who Pacifies the North Murong Long said to Bao, "Though Tuoba Gui has repeatedly gained small advantages, he has halted his army for a year; his fierce momentum is broken and bent, horses and men dead and wounded beyond half, men's hearts think of return, the various tribes are scattered—this is precisely the time he can be broken.

sentences.zh: 加之舉城思奮，若因我之銳，乘彼之衰，往無不克。

translations.literal: Moreover, the whole city burns to strike; if we take our sharpness and ride their decline, we go forth and nothing fails to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the whole city burns to strike; if we take our sharpness and ride their decline, we go forth and nothing fails to be taken.

sentences.zh: 如其持重不決，將卒氣喪，日益困逼，事久變生，後雖欲用之，不可得也，！」

translations.literal: If you hold back and do not decide, generals and soldiers will lose spirit, daily more pressed and besieged; after long delay change will arise—later, even if you wish to use them, you cannot obtain them!"
translations.idiomatic: If you hold back and do not decide, generals and soldiers will lose spirit, daily more pressed and besieged; after long delay change will arise—later, even if you wish to use them, you cannot obtain them!"

sentences.zh: 寶然之。

translations.literal: Bao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao agreed.

sentences.zh: 而衛大將軍麟每沮其議，隆成列而罷者，前後數四。

translations.literal: But the Grand General of the Guard Lin always thwarted the plan; Long arrayed his ranks and withdrew, before and after, four or five times.
translations.idiomatic: But the Grand General of the Guard Murong Lin always thwarted the plan; Long arrayed his ranks and withdrew, before and after, four or five times.

sentences.zh: 寶使人請於魏王珪，欲還其弟觚，割常山以西皆與魏以求和。

translations.literal: Bao sent someone to ask King Gui of Wei, wishing to return his younger brother Gou, ceding all west of Changshan to Wei to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sent someone to ask King Tuoba Gui of Wei, wishing to return his younger brother Murong Gou, ceding all west of Changshan to Wei to seek peace.

sentences.zh: 珪許之；

translations.literal: Gui agreed;
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed;

sentences.zh: 既而寶悔之。

translations.literal: Presently Bao regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Murong Bao regretted the agreement.

sentences.zh: 己酉，珪如盧奴，辛亥，復圍中山。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Gui went to Lunu; on xinhai, he again besieged Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Tuoba Gui went to Lunu; on xinhai, he again besieged Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 燕將士數千人俱自請於寶曰：「今坐守窮城，終於困弊，臣等願得一出樂戰，而陛下每抑之，此為坐自摧敗也。

translations.literal: Several thousand Yan officers and soldiers together petitioned Bao, saying, "Now we sit guarding a doomed city and will end in exhaustion and ruin; we wish we could sally forth once and fight with joy, yet Your Majesty always restrains us—this is to sit and destroy ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Yan officers and soldiers petitioned Murong Bao together, saying, "We sit in this doomed city until we are spent, yet we are denied a sortie—we are being destroyed by our own passivity.

sentences.zh: 且受圍歷時，無他奇變，徒望積久寇賊自退。

translations.literal: Moreover, we have been besieged for a long time with no other stratagem but to hope that in time the invaders will withdraw on their own.
translations.idiomatic: They had been under siege for a long time with no stratagem but to hope the enemy would eventually withdraw.

sentences.zh: 今內外之勢，強弱懸絕，彼必不自退明矣，宜從眾一決。」

translations.literal: Now the inner and outer situation, strong and weak, are poles apart; it is clear they will certainly not withdraw on their own—you should follow the multitude in one decisive move."
translations.idiomatic: The balance of power inside and out is hopeless; the enemy will not leave of their own accord—the court should heed them and fight."

sentences.zh: 寶許之。

translations.literal: Bao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao agreed.

sentences.zh: 隆退而勒兵，召諸參佐謂之曰：「皇威不振，寇賊內侮，臣子同恥，義不顧生。

translations.literal: Long withdrew and mustered the troops; he summoned his staff and said to them, "Imperial majesty is not restored; bandits insult us within; ministers and subjects share the shame—we do not spare our lives in duty.
translations.idiomatic: Long withdrew to muster troops and told his staff, "The throne is humbled and the enemy is inside the walls; we share this shame and owe our lives to the state.

sentences.zh: 今幸而破賊，吉還固善；

translations.literal: Now if we are fortunate and break the enemy, a safe return is well;
translations.idiomatic: If we break the enemy, we return in honor;

sentences.zh: 若其不幸，亦使吾志節獲展。

translations.literal: if we are not fortunate, our integrity and resolve will still be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, our loyalty will still be proved.

sentences.zh: 卿等有北見吾母者，為吾道此情也！」

translations.literal: If any of you should see my mother in the north, convey this feeling for me!"
translations.idiomatic: If any of you reach my mother in the north, tell her this!"

sentences.zh: 乃被甲上馬，詣門俟命。

translations.literal: He then donned armor, mounted, and went to the gate to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: He donned armor, mounted, and waited at the gate for orders.

sentences.zh: 麟復固止寶，眾大忿恨，隆涕泣而還。

translations.literal: Lin again firmly stopped Bao; the crowd was greatly resentful; Long wept and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin blocked Bao again; the soldiers seethed with anger; Long returned in tears.

sentences.zh: 是夜，麟以兵劫左衛將軍北地王精，使帥禁兵弒寶。

translations.literal: That night, Lin used troops to coerce the Left Guard General, the Prince of Beidi, Jing, making him lead the palace guard to assassinate Bao.
translations.idiomatic: That night, Murong Lin coerced the Left Guard General, Prince of Beidi Murong Jing, to lead the palace guard in assassinating Bao.

sentences.zh: 精以義拒之，麟怒，殺精，出奔西山，依丁零餘眾。

translations.literal: Jing refused on grounds of righteousness; Lin was angry, killed Jing, fled to the western hills, and relied on the remnant Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Jing refused on grounds of loyalty; Lin killed him, fled to the western hills, and joined remnant Dingling forces.

sentences.zh: 於是城中人情震駭。

translations.literal: At this the hearts of the people in the city were shaken in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The city was thrown into terror.

sentences.zh: 寶不知麟所之，以清河王會軍在近，恐麟奪會軍，先據龍城，乃召隆及驃騎大將軍農，謀去中山，走保龍城。

translations.literal: Bao did not know where Lin had gone; the Prince of Qinghe Hui army was near, and he feared Lin would seize Hui army first and occupy Longcheng; he therefore summoned Long and the General of Agile Cavalry Nong to plan leaving Zhongshan and fleeing to hold Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing Lin whereabouts and fearing Lin would seize Prince Qinghe Murong Hui nearby army, Bao summoned Long and General of Agile Cavalry Murong Nong to flee Zhongshan for Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 隆曰「先帝櫛風沐雨以成中興之業，崩未期年而天下大壞，豈得不謂之孤負邪！

translations.literal: Long said, "The late emperor braved wind and rain to accomplish the restoration; he has been dead less than a year and the realm is utterly broken—can this be called anything but betrayal of his trust?
translations.idiomatic: Long said, "The late emperor rebuilt the state through hardship; within a year all is ruin—have we not betrayed him?

sentences.zh: 今外寇方盛而內難復起，骨肉乘離，百姓疑懼，誠不可以拒敵；

translations.literal: Now foreign invaders are at their peak and internal troubles have risen again; flesh and blood turn on one another, and the people are doubtful and afraid—truly we cannot resist the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Invaders press us while kin turn on kin; the people are afraid—we cannot hold the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 北遷舊都，亦事之宜。

translations.literal: to move north to the old capital is also fitting in the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Retreating north to the old capital is reasonable.

sentences.zh: 然龍川地狹民貧，若以中國之意取足其中，復朝夕望有大功，此必不可。

translations.literal: Yet Longchuan land is narrow and its people poor; if you seek to satisfy the heart of the Central Plains there, and morning and evening still look for great achievement, this certainly cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: But Longcheng is poor and small; you cannot expect central-China grandeur there overnight.

sentences.zh: 若節用愛民，務農訓兵，數年之中，公私充實，而趙、魏之間，厭苦寇暴，民思燕德，庶幾返旆，克復故業。

translations.literal: If you economize and cherish the people, devote yourself to agriculture and drill the army, within several years public and private stores will be full; between Zhao and Wei the people, weary of bandit cruelty, will long for Yan virtue—perhaps you may turn the banners and recover the old enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Frugality, farming, and training may refill the realm; the people of Zhao and Wei, sick of Wei violence, may yet welcome Yan back.

sentences.zh: 如其未能，則憑險自固，猶足以優遊養銳耳。」

translations.literal: If that cannot be done, then holding fast in defensible terrain is still enough to rest and nurture strength at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: If not, holding the mountains still lets you recover strength."

sentences.zh: 寶曰：「卿言盡理，騰一從卿意耳。」

translations.literal: Bao said, "Your words are entirely reasonable; I will wholly follow your intent."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said, "You are right—I will do as you advise."

sentences.zh: 遼東高撫，善卜筮，素為隆所信厚，私謂隆曰：「殿下北行，終不能達，太妃亦不可得見。

translations.literal: Gao Fu of Liaodong, skilled in divination, was long trusted by Long; he said privately to Long, "If the Prince goes north, in the end you will not arrive, and you will not be able to see the consort dowager either.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Fu of Liaodong, a diviner Long trusted, whispered to him, "If you go north you will never arrive—and never see your mother.

sentences.zh: 若使主上獨往，殿下潛留於此，必有大功。」

translations.literal: If you let the sovereign go alone while you stay here in secret, there will certainly be great merit."
translations.idiomatic: Stay while the emperor flees alone, and great merit will be yours."

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「國有大難，主上蒙塵，且老母在北，吾得北首而死，猶無所恨。

translations.literal: Long said, "The state has great trouble; the sovereign suffers exile; moreover my old mother is in the north—for me to die facing north still leaves no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Long replied, "The realm is in crisis and my lord is in exile; my mother is in the north—to die facing her is enough for me.

sentences.zh: 卿是何言也！」

translations.literal: What words are these of yours!"
translations.idiomatic: What kind of talk is that!"

sentences.zh: 乃遍召僚佐，問其去留，唯司馬魯恭、參軍成岌願從，餘皆欲留，隆並聽之。

translations.literal: He then summoned all his staff and asked who would go or stay; only the marshal Lu Gong and the aide Cheng Ji wished to follow; the rest all wished to stay, and Long permitted them all.
translations.idiomatic: He asked his staff who would follow; only Lu Gong and Cheng Ji would go—the rest he allowed to stay.

sentences.zh: 農部將谷會歸說農曰：「城中之人，皆涉珪、參合所殺者父兄子弟，泣血踴躍，欲與魏戰，而為衛軍所抑。

translations.literal: Gu Hui, a subordinate of Nong, returned and said to Nong, "The people in the city are all those whose fathers, brothers, and sons were killed at Shegui and Canhe; they weep blood and leap in rage, wishing to fight Wei, yet are suppressed by the Grand General of the Guard."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Hui told Nong, "The garrison is full of men whose kin died at Canhe; they thirst to fight Wei but Lin holds them back.

sentences.zh: 今聞主上當北遷，皆曰：『得慕容氏一人奉而立之，以與魏戰，死無所恨。』

translations.literal: Now hearing that the sovereign is to move north, all say, "If we could get one man of the Murong clan to install and lead us, we would fight Wei and death would hold no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the emperor will flee north, they say they would die gladly if any Murong prince stayed to lead them."

sentences.zh: 大王幸而留此，以副眾望，擊退魏軍，撫寧畿甸，奉迎大駕，亦不失為忠臣也。」

translations.literal: If the great prince would stay here to fulfill their hope, strike the Wei army, pacify the capital region, and welcome back the imperial carriage, you would still not fail to be a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Stay, defeat Wei, pacify the region, and welcome the emperor back—you would still be a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 農欲殺歸而惜其材力，謂之曰：「必如此以望生，不如就死！」

translations.literal: Nong wished to kill Hui but valued his ability; he said to him, "To hope for life by such means—better to seek death at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Nong nearly killed him but said, "To hope to live that way—you might as well die now!"

sentences.zh: 壬子，夜，寶與太子策、遼西王農、高陽王隆、長樂王盛等萬餘騎出赴會軍，河間王熙、勃海王朗、博陵王鑒皆幼，不能出城，隆還入迎之，自為鞁乘，俱得免。

translations.literal: On renzi, at night, Bao with the crown prince Ce, the Prince of Liaoxi Nong, the Prince of Gaoyang Long, the Prince of Changle Sheng, and others—more than ten thousand horsemen—rode out to join Hui army; the Princes of Hejian Xi, Bohai Lang, and Boling Jian were young and could not leave the city; Long went back in to fetch them, himself holding the saddle, and all escaped.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi at night Bao fled with the crown prince, Nong, Long, Sheng, and ten thousand horsemen; young princes Xi, Lang, and Jian could not leave until Long fetched them on his own saddle.

sentences.zh: 燕將王沈等隆降魏。

translations.literal: The Yan generals Wang Shen and others surrendered to Wei in droves.
translations.idiomatic: Yan generals including Wang Shen surrendered to Wei in droves.

sentences.zh: 樂浪王惠、中書侍郎韓范、員外郎段宏、太史令劉起等帥工伎三百奔鄴。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lelang Hui, the Master of Writing Han Fan, the attendant Duan Hong, the grand astrologer Liu Qi, and others led three hundred artisans and fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lelang Murong Hui, Han Fan, Duan Hong, Liu Qi, and others fled to Ye with three hundred artisans.

sentences.zh: 中山城中無主，百姓惶惑，東門不閉。

translations.literal: Within Zhongshan there was no ruler; the people were fearful and uncertain; the eastern gate was not closed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan was left without a ruler; panic spread and the eastern gate stood open.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪欲夜入城，冠軍將軍王建志在虜掠，乃言恐士卒盜府庫物，請俟明旦，珪乃止。

translations.literal: King Gui of Wei wished to enter the city by night; the General Who Establishes the State Wang Jian, intent on plundering the enemy, said he feared the soldiers would rob the treasury and asked to wait until dawn; Gui then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui meant to enter by night, but Wang Jian, eager to loot, claimed the troops would plunder the treasury and delayed him until dawn.

sentences.zh: 燕開封公詳從寶不及，城中立以為主，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: Yan Duke of Kaifeng, Xiang, could not keep up with Bao; the city installed him as ruler and shut the gates to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Kaifeng Murong Xiang, left behind, was made ruler and shut the gates to resist.

sentences.zh: 珪盡眾攻之，連日不拔，使人登巢車，臨城諭之曰：「慕容寶已棄汝走，汝曹百姓空自取死，欲誰為乎？」

translations.literal: Gui mustered his host to attack; for days he could not take it; he had men mount nest carts, overlook the city, and announce, "Murong Bao has abandoned you and fled—why do you common people empty yourselves in death; for whom do you act?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui besieged Xiang for days, then called from nest carts: "Murong Bao has fled—why die for nothing?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「群小無知，恐復如參合之眾，故苟延旬月之命耳。」

translations.literal: They all said, "We petty men are ignorant, fearing we shall again be like the host at Canhe; therefore we merely prolong our lives for a month or so."
translations.idiomatic: The people answered, "We fear another Canhe massacre—that is why we cling to life a little longer."

sentences.zh: 珪顧王建唾其面，使中領將軍長孫肥、左將軍李栗將三千騎追寶至范陽，不及，破其新城戍而還。

translations.literal: Gui looked at Wang Jian and spat in his face; he sent the Central Commander-in-Chief Zhangsun Fei and the Left General Li Li with three thousand horsemen to pursue Bao to Fanyang; they did not overtake him, broke his garrison at Xincheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gui spat in Wang Jian face and sent Zhangsun Fei and Li Li to pursue Bao to Fanyang; they missed him but destroyed his garrison at Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，尊皇太后李氏為太皇太后。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the empress dowager Lady Li was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Empress Dowager Lady Li was elevated to grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 戊午，立皇后王氏。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Lady Wang was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Lady Wang was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶出中山，與趙王麟遇於□開城，麟不意寶至，驚駭，帥其眾奔蒲陰，復出屯望都，土人頗供給之。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Bao left Zhongshan and met the Prince of Zhao Lin at Kaicheng; Lin did not expect Bao to come, was startled, led his host to flee to Puyin, then came out again to camp at Wangdu, and the local people supplied him fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Zhongshan, Bao met Prince Zhao Murong Lin at Kaicheng; Lin fled to Puyin in alarm, then camped at Wangdu, where locals fed his men.

sentences.zh: 慕容詳遣兵掩擊麟，獲其妻子，麟脫走入山。

translations.literal: Murong Xiang sent troops in a surprise attack on Lin, captured his wife and children, and Lin escaped alone into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xiang raided Lin, seized his family, and Lin fled into the hills alone.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，寶至薊，殿中親近散亡略盡，惟高陽王隆所領數百騎為宿衛。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Bao reached Ji; the close attendants of the palace had scattered almost entirely—only the several hundred horsemen led by the Prince of Gaoyang Long remained as night guard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Bao reached Ji; his court attendants had nearly all fled—only Long few hundred horsemen guarded him.

sentences.zh: 清河王會帥騎卒二萬迎於薊南，寶怪會容止怏怏有恨色，密告隆及遼西王農。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qinghe Hui led twenty thousand horsemen to welcome him south of Ji; Bao thought Hui bearing sullen and resentful, and secretly told Long and the Prince of Liaoxi Nong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qinghe Murong Hui met him south of Ji with twenty thousand horse; Bao found his manner sullen and told Nong and Long in secret.

sentences.zh: 農、隆俱曰：「會年少，專任方面，習驕所致，豈有它也！

translations.literal: Nong and Long both said, "Hui is young, holding sole command in a region—habit has made him proud; how could there be anything else!
translations.idiomatic: Nong and Long said, "He is young and commands a region alone—pride is natural, not treason.

sentences.zh: 臣等當以禮責之。」

translations.literal: We shall reprove him with ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: We will rebuke him properly."

sentences.zh: 寶雖從之，然猶詔解會兵以屬隆，隆固辭；

translations.literal: Bao followed them, yet still ordered Hui army detached and assigned to Long; Long firmly declined;
translations.idiomatic: Bao accepted this but still stripped Hui of his troops for Long, who refused;

sentences.zh: 乃減會兵分給農、隆。

translations.literal: he then reduced Hui army and divided it between Nong and Long.
translations.idiomatic: he divided Hui forces between Nong and Long instead.

sentences.zh: 又遣西可公庫辱官驥帥兵三千助守中山。

translations.literal: He also sent the Western Kegong Kuluo Guan Ji with three thousand men to help defend Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Kuluo Guan Ji with three thousand men to reinforce Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，寶盡徙薊中府庫北趣龍城。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Bao moved all stores of Ji north toward Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Bao moved Ji treasury north toward Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏石河頭引兵追之，戊午，及寶於夏謙澤。

translations.literal: Wei Shi Hetou led troops in pursuit; on wuwu he caught Bao at Xiaqian Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hetou of Wei pursued and on wuwu caught Bao at Xiaqian Marsh.

sentences.zh: 寶不欲戰，清河王會曰：「臣撫教士卒，惟敵是求。

translations.literal: Bao did not wish to fight; the Prince of Qinghe Hui said, "Your servant has trained and taught the soldiers to seek only the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Bao wished to avoid battle; Hui said, "I have trained these men for no purpose but to fight.

sentences.zh: 今大駕蒙塵，人思效命，而虜敢自送，眾心忿憤。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage suffers exile and men think of giving their lives; yet the barbarians dare deliver themselves—the hearts of the host are furious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is in exile and every man yearns to repay Wei—the enemy has offered themselves.

sentences.zh: 《兵法》曰：『歸師勿遏。』

translations.literal: The Art of War says, "Do not intercept a returning army."
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says, "Do not intercept a returning army."

sentences.zh: 又曰『置之死地而後生。』

translations.literal: It also says, "Place them on death ground and they will live."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Place them on death ground and they will live."

sentences.zh: 今我皆得之，何患不克！

translations.literal: Now we have obtained both—what worry is there of not prevailing!
translations.idiomatic: We have both now—how can we fail?

sentences.zh: 若其捨去，賊必乘人，或生餘變。」

translations.literal: If we let them go, the bandits will surely take advantage of men weakness, or other changes may arise."
translations.idiomatic: If we let them go, Wei will strike when we weaken—or worse may follow."

sentences.zh: 寶乃從之。

translations.literal: Bao then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao agreed.

sentences.zh: 會整陳與魏兵戰，農、隆等將南來騎沖之，魏兵大敗，追奔百餘里，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Hui arrayed his ranks and fought the Wei army; Nong, Long, and the others led the southern cavalry in a charge; the Wei army was greatly defeated; they pursued more than a hundred li and took several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Hui formed line and shattered the Wei army; Nong and Long charged with the southern horse; Wei fled a hundred li with thousands slain.

sentences.zh: 隆又獨追數十里而還，謂故吏留台治書陽璆曰：「中山城中積兵數萬，不得展吾意，今日之捷，令人遺恨。」

translations.literal: Long again pursued alone for several tens of li; on returning he said to Yang Qiu, the reviewing secretary left at the capital, "In Zhongshan tens of thousands of troops were massed yet I could not deploy my intent; today victory leaves regret."
translations.idiomatic: Long pursued alone for tens of li and told Yang Qiu, "Zhongshan held tens of thousands yet I could not fight as I wished—today victory still grieves me."

sentences.zh: 因慷慨流涕。

translations.literal: He thereupon sighed and wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He wept in frustration.

sentences.zh: 會既敗魏兵，矜很滋甚；

translations.literal: After Hui had defeated the Wei army, his arrogance grew ever greater;
translations.idiomatic: After this victory Hui grew insufferably proud;

sentences.zh: 隆屢訓責之，會益忿恚。

translations.literal: Long repeatedly admonished and reproved him, and Hui grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Long rebuked him repeatedly, deepening his resentment.

sentences.zh: 會以農、隆皆嘗鎮龍城，屬尊位重，名望素出己右，恐至龍城，權政不復在己，已知終無為嗣之望，乃謀作亂。

translations.literal: Because Nong and Long had both once held Longcheng, were of honored rank and heavy standing, and their fame had always exceeded his, he feared that on reaching Longcheng power would no longer be his; knowing in the end he had no hope of succession, he plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and Long had ruled Longcheng before, outranked him, and enjoyed greater fame; fearing loss of power at Longcheng and despairing of the succession, he plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 幽、平之兵皆懷會恩，不樂屬二王，請於寶曰：「清河王勇略高世，臣等與之誓同生死，願陛下與皇太子、諸王留薊宮，臣等從王南解京師之圍，還迎大駕。」

translations.literal: The soldiers of You and Ping all cherished Hui kindness and did not wish to serve the two princes; they asked Bao, "The Prince of Qinghe courage and strategy surpass his age; we have sworn life and death with him—we beg Your Majesty and the crown prince and princes to remain in the Ji palace while we follow the prince south to raise the siege of the capital and return to welcome the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Troops from You and Ping, loyal to Hui, asked Bao to keep the court at Ji while they followed Hui south to relieve Zhongshan."

sentences.zh: 寶左右皆惡會，言於寶曰：「清河王不得為太子，神色甚不平。

translations.literal: Those around Bao all hated Hui and said to Bao, "The Prince of Qinghe cannot be crown prince; his expression is very discontented.
translations.idiomatic: “Bao attendants, hostile to Hui, said he could never be heir and looked mutinous.

sentences.zh: 且其才武過人，善收人心；

translations.literal: Moreover his talent and martial prowess surpass others, and he is skilled at winning men hearts;
translations.idiomatic: His talent and charisma exceed others—

sentences.zh: 陛下若從眾請，臣恐解圍之後，必有衛輒之事。」

translations.literal: if Your Majesty follows the multitude request, this servant fears that after the siege is raised there may be a matter like Wei Zhe."
translations.idiomatic: if you give him an independent command, after Zhongshan falls you may face a Wei Zhe affair."

sentences.zh: 寶乃謂眾曰：「道通年少，才不及二王，豈可當專征之任！

translations.literal: Bao then said to the crowd, "Daotong is young; his talent does not match the two princes—how can he bear sole command on campaign!
translations.idiomatic: Bao told the soldiers, "Hui is young and less able than Nong and Long—he cannot command alone.

sentences.zh: 且朕方自統六師，杖會以為羽翼，何可離左右也！」

translations.literal: Moreover I myself am about to take the field with the six armies and use Hui as my wing—how can he leave my side!"
translations.idiomatic: I will lead the host myself and keep him at my side—how can he leave me?"

sentences.zh: 眾不悅而退。

translations.literal: The crowd withdrew displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers withdrew in discontent.

sentences.zh: 左右勸寶殺會，侍御史仇尼歸聞之，告會曰：「大王所恃者父，父已異圖；

translations.literal: Those around Bao urged him to kill Hui; the attendant censor Qiu Ni Gui heard of it and told Hui, "What the great prince relies on is your father, and your father already harbors other designs;
translations.idiomatic: Attendants urged Bao to kill Hui; Qiu Ni Gui warned Hui, "You rely on your father, but he already plots against you;

sentences.zh: 所杖者兵，兵已去手；

translations.literal: what you lean on is your army, and your army is already taken from your hand;
translations.idiomatic: your army is already being stripped away;

sentences.zh: 欲於何所自容乎？

translations.literal: on what ground will you contain yourself?
translations.idiomatic: where will you stand?

sentences.zh: 不如誅二王，廢太子，大王自處東宮，兼將相之任，以匡復社稷，此上策也。」

translations.literal: Better to kill the two princes, depose the crown prince, have the great prince install yourself in the Eastern Palace and take both minister and general charge together, to restore the altars of state—this is the upper stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Kill Nong and Long, depose the crown prince, seize the Eastern Palace and command—restore the state—that is the best course."

sentences.zh: 會猶豫，未許。

translations.literal: Hui hesitated and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Hui hesitated.

sentences.zh: 寶謂農、隆曰：「觀道通志趣，必反無疑，宜早除之。」

translations.literal: Bao said to Nong and Long, "Judging Daotong intent, he is certain to rebel without doubt—you should kill him early."
translations.idiomatic: Bao told Nong and Long, "Hui will rebel—kill him now."

sentences.zh: 農、隆曰：「今寇敵內侮，中土紛紜，社稷之危，有如累卵。

translations.literal: Nong and Long said, "Now invaders insult us within and the central realm is in turmoil; the danger to the altars of state is like eggs piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Invaders press in and the realm totters like a pile of eggs.

sentences.zh: 會鎮撫舊都，遠赴國難，其威名之重，足以震動四鄰。

translations.literal: Hui pacifies the old capital and has come far to the state peril; the weight of his fame is enough to shake the four neighboring realms.
translations.idiomatic: Hui held the north and rode to the crisis; his fame steadies the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 逆狀未彰而遽殺之，豈徒傷父子恩，亦恐大損威望。」

translations.literal: To kill him hastily when his treason is not yet manifest will not only wound the grace between father and son but also greatly damage prestige."
translations.idiomatic: To kill him before guilt is clear wounds father and son and shatters morale."

sentences.zh: 寶曰：「會逆志已成，卿等慈恕，不忍早殺，恐一旦為變，必先害諸父，然後及吾，至時勿悔自負也！」

translations.literal: Bao said, "Hui rebellious intent is already formed; you are kindly and forgiving, unwilling to kill him early—I fear that one morning when mutiny breaks out he will first harm the various fathers and then reach me; when that time comes do not regret and blame yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao said, "His treason is set; your mercy will let him strike the princes first, then me—do not regret it then!"

sentences.zh: 會聞之，益懼。

translations.literal: When Hui heard of it, he grew ever more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Hui grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸酉，寶宿廣都黃榆谷。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, guiyou; Bao lodged at Huangyu Valley in Guangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiyou, Bao camped at Huangyu Valley in Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 會遣其黨仇尼歸、吳提染干帥壯士二十餘人分道襲農、隆，殺隆於賬下；

translations.literal: Hui sent his partisans Qiu Ni Gui and Wu Ti Ran Gan with more than twenty stout fellows each by separate routes to strike Nong and Long; Long was killed beneath his tent;
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Qiu Ni Gui and Wu Ti Ran Gan with twenty braves each to assassinate Nong and Long; Long was killed in his tent;

sentences.zh: 農被重創，執仇尼歸，逃入山中。

translations.literal: Nong was heavily wounded, seized Qiu Ni Gui, and fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Nong was gravely wounded, seized Qiu Ni Gui, and fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 會以仇尼歸被執，事終顯發，乃夜詣寶曰：「農、隆謀逆，臣已除之。」

translations.literal: Because Qiu Ni Gui was seized and the affair would in the end be exposed, at night he went to Bao and said, "Nong and Long plotted rebellion; your servant has already removed them."
translations.idiomatic: With Ni Gui captured, Hui went to Bao at night claiming he had killed rebel princes Nong and Long."

sentences.zh: 寶欲討會，陽為好言以安之曰：「吾固疑二王久矣，除之甚善。」

translations.literal: Bao wished to punish Hui and pretended to reassure him with kind words, saying, "I had long suspected the two princes; removing them is very good.
translations.idiomatic: Bao pretended approval: "I long suspected them—well done.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，旦，會立仗嚴備，乃引道。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, at dawn, Hui drew up his guard in full array and then led the march.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu at dawn Hui marched with full escort.

sentences.zh: 會欲棄隆喪，餘崇涕泣固請，乃聽載隨軍，農出，自歸，寶呵之曰：「何以自負邪！」

translations.literal: Hui wished to abandon Long coffin; Yu Chong wept and firmly begged, and he was allowed to load it with the army; Nong came out and returned of himself; Bao rebuked him, saying, "Why have you betrayed yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui would have left Long coffin until Yu Chong tears made him take it along; Nong returned wounded; Bao scolded him, "How could you betray us?"

sentences.zh: 命執之。

translations.literal: He ordered him seized.
translations.idiomatic: He had Nong seized.

sentences.zh: 行十餘里，寶顧召群臣食，且議農罪。

translations.literal: After marching more than ten li, Bao looked back and summoned the ministers to eat and discuss Nong crime.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li on, Bao halted to dine and try Nong.

sentences.zh: 會就坐，寶目衛軍將軍慕輿騰使斬會，傷其首，不能殺。

translations.literal: Hui took his seat; Bao signaled the General of the Guard Murong Teng to behead Hui; he wounded his head but could not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: As Hui sat down, Bao signaled Murong Teng to strike; Teng wounded but failed to kill him.

sentences.zh: 會走赴其軍，勒兵攻寶。

translations.literal: Hui ran to his army, mustered troops, and attacked Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fled to his troops and attacked Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶帥數百騎馳二百里，晡時，至龍城。

translations.literal: Bao led several hundred horsemen in a gallop of two hundred li; at the hour of shen he reached Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bao galloped two hundred li with a few hundred horse and reached Longcheng by evening.

sentences.zh: 會遣騎追至石城，不及。

translations.literal: Hui sent cavalry in pursuit to Shicheng but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui's pursuers reached Shicheng but failed to catch Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，會遣仇尼歸攻龍城；

translations.literal: On yihai, Hui sent Qiu Ni to attack Longcheng;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Murong Hui sent Qiu Ni to assault Longcheng;

sentences.zh: 寶夜遣兵襲擊，破之。

translations.literal: Bao sent troops by night in a surprise attack and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao struck by night and routed them.

sentences.zh: 會遣使請誅左右佞臣，並求為太子；

translations.literal: Hui sent envoys requesting execution of the sycophants at his side, and also asking to be made crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui sent envoys demanding the execution of Bao's favorites and asking to be named crown prince;

sentences.zh: 寶不許。

translations.literal: Bao did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao refused.

sentences.zh: 會盡收乘輿器服，以後宮分給將帥，署置百官，自稱皇太子、錄尚書事，引兵向龍城，以討慕輿騰為名；

translations.literal: Hui seized all imperial carriage accoutrements and robes, distributed the inner palace among his generals, appointed officials, styled himself crown prince and Recorder of the Imperial Secretariat, led troops toward Longcheng under the pretext of punishing Murong Teng;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui seized the imperial regalia, divided the harem among his officers, set up a rival court as crown prince and chief minister, and marched on Longcheng claiming to punish Murong Teng;

sentences.zh: 丙子，頓兵城下。

translations.literal: On bingzi, he halted his army below the city.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, he encamped beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 寶臨西門，會乘馬遙與寶語，寶責讓之。

translations.literal: Bao came to the west gate; Hui mounted a horse and spoke with Bao from afar; Bao reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao appeared at the west gate; Murong Hui rode up and shouted across to him; Bao rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 會命軍士向寶大噪以耀威，城中將士皆憤怒，向暮出戰，大破之，會兵死傷太半，走還營。

translations.literal: Hui ordered his soldiers to shout loudly at Bao to display might; the officers and soldiers in the city were all enraged; toward evening they sallied forth and inflicted a great defeat; more than half of Hui's army was killed or wounded, and they fled back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had his men jeer at Bao to intimidate him; the garrison erupted in fury and sallied at dusk, shattering his army—more than half his force was lost as they fled to camp.

sentences.zh: 侍御郎高雲夜帥敢死士百餘人襲會軍，會眾皆潰。

translations.literal: Attendant Gao Yun by night led more than a hundred dare-to-die soldiers in a surprise attack on Hui's army; Hui's host all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gao Yun led a hundred suicide troops in a night raid; Hui's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 會將十餘騎奔中山，開封公詳殺之。

translations.literal: Hui fled with a dozen or so horsemen to Zhongshan; the Duke of Kaifeng, Xiang, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui fled with a dozen riders toward Zhongshan; the Duke of Kaifeng Murong Xiang killed him.

sentences.zh: 寶殺會母及其三子。

translations.literal: Bao killed Hui's mother and his three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao executed Hui's mother and three sons.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，寶大赦，凡與會同謀者，皆除罪，復舊職。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Bao proclaimed a general amnesty; all who had plotted with Hui had their crimes cleared and were restored to their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Murong Bao declared a general amnesty, pardoning all who had joined Hui and restoring them to office.

sentences.zh: 論功行賞，拜將軍、封侯者數百人。

translations.literal: Rewards were distributed according to merit; several hundred were appointed generals and enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was rewarded with hundreds of promotions to general and enfeoffment as marquises.

sentences.zh: 遼西王農骨破見腦，寶手自裹創，僅而獲濟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liaoxi, Nong, had a skull fracture with brain exposed; Bao personally wrapped the wound; he barely survived.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Liaoxi Murong Nong's skull was split open with brain showing; Murong Bao bandaged the wound himself; Nong barely survived.

sentences.zh: 以農為左僕射，尋拜司空、領尚書令。

translations.literal: Nong was made Left Vice Director; soon after he was appointed Grand Minister of Works and concurrently Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Nong was made Left Vice Director, then soon Grand Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 餘崇出自歸，寶嘉其忠，拜中堅將軍，使典宿衛。

translations.literal: Yu Chong came forward to surrender; Bao commended his loyalty, made him General of the Central Guard, and put him in charge of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chong surrendered voluntarily; Bao praised his loyalty, made him General of the Central Guard, and put him over the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 贈高陽王隆司徒，謚曰康。

translations.literal: The late Prince of Gaoyang, Long, was posthumously made Grand Minister of Works with the posthumous title Kang ("Peaceful").
translations.idiomatic: The late Prince of Gaoyang Murong Long was posthumously honored as Grand Minister of Works with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 寶以高雲為建威將軍，封夕陽公，養以為子。

translations.literal: Bao made Gao Yun General Who Establishes Might, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xiyang, and adopted him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao made Gao Yun General Who Establishes Might, Duke of Xiyang, and adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 雲，高句麗之支屬也，燕王皝破高句麗，徙於青山，由是世為燕臣。

translations.literal: Gao Yun was a branch descendant of Goguryeo; when Yan King Huang defeated Goguryeo, they were moved to Qingshan; from then on they served Yan for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun was a collateral line of Goguryeo; after Yan King Murong Huang conquered Goguryeo and moved them to Qingshan, his family served Yan for generations.

sentences.zh: 雲沉厚寡言，時人莫知，惟中衛將軍長樂馮跋奇其志度，與之為友。

translations.literal: Gao Yun was deep and taciturn; contemporaries did not know him; only Central Guard General Feng Ba of Changle marveled at his ambition and capacity, and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun was grave and quiet; few knew him; only Central Guard General Feng Ba of Changle saw his depth and became his friend.

sentences.zh: 跋父和，事西燕王永，為將軍，永敗，徙和龍。

translations.literal: Feng Ba's father He had served Western Yan's Wang Yong as a general; when Yong was defeated, they were moved to Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba's father He had served Western Yan's Wang Yong; after Yong's defeat they were resettled at Helong.

sentences.zh: 僕射王國寶、建威將軍王緒依附會稽王道子，納賄窮奢，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Vice Director Wang Guobao and General Who Establishes Might Wang Xu attached themselves to Kuaiji Prince Daozi, taking bribes to live in boundless extravagance beyond all measure.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Guobao and General Who Establishes Might Wang Xu clung to Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi, taking bribes and living in boundless luxury.

sentences.zh: 惡王恭、殷仲堪，勸道子裁損其兵權；

translations.literal: They hated Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan, and urged Daozi to cut back their military authority;
translations.idiomatic: They hated Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan and urged Daozi to strip them of military power;

sentences.zh: 中外恟恟不安。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court there was anxious unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Anxiety spread through court and country.

sentences.zh: 恭等各繕甲勒兵，表請北伐；

translations.literal: Gong and the others each repaired armor and mustered troops, memorializing to request a northern campaign;
translations.idiomatic: Gong and the others armed their men and memorialized for a northern expedition;

sentences.zh: 道子疑之，詔以盛夏妨農，悉使解嚴。

translations.literal: Daozi was suspicious and issued an edict that the height of summer would harm farming, ordering them all to stand down.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi, suspicious, ordered them all to stand down on the pretext that summer campaigning would harm the harvest.

sentences.zh: 恭遣使與仲堪謀討國寶等。

translations.literal: Gong sent envoys to plot with Zhongkan to attack Guobao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong sent envoys to Yin Zhongkan to plot against Guobao and his faction.

sentences.zh: 桓玄以仁不得志，欲假仲堪兵勢以作亂，乃說仲堪曰：「國寶與君諸人素已為對，唯患相斃之不速耳。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan, having failed to achieve his ambitions, wished to borrow Zhongkan's military strength to raise rebellion; he therefore said to Zhongkan: "Guobao and you others have long been opposed; they only worry that you will not destroy each other quickly enough.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan, frustrated in his ambitions, hoped to use Yin Zhongkan's armies to rebel; he told Zhongkan, "Guobao and your party have long been enemies—they only wish you would destroy one another faster.

sentences.zh: 今既執大權，與王緒相表裡，其所回易，無不如志；

translations.literal: Now that they hold great power, working inside and outside with Wang Xu, whatever they turn their hand to goes as they wish;
translations.idiomatic: Now they hold real power, inside and out with Wang Xu, and nothing they want is denied;

sentences.zh: 孝伯居元舅之地，必未敢害之。

translations.literal: Xiao Bo occupies the position of imperial maternal uncle—they surely dare not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong as the emperor's maternal uncle is probably safe from them.

sentences.zh: 君為先帝所拔，超居方任，人情皆以君為雖有思致，非方伯才。

translations.literal: You were raised up by the late emperor and hold a frontier post beyond your due; popular opinion holds that although you have ideas, you are not fit to be a regional governor.
translations.idiomatic: You were promoted by the late emperor beyond your station; people say you have wit but not the talent of a frontier governor.

sentences.zh: 彼若發詔征君為中書令，用殷覬為荊州，君何以處之？」

translations.literal: If they issue an edict summoning you to be Director of the Secretariat and appoint Yin Kai as Governor of Jingzhou, how will you respond?"
translations.idiomatic: If they summon you to the Secretariat and put Yin Kai in charge of Jingzhou, what will you do?"

sentences.zh: 仲堪曰：「憂之久矣，計將安出？」

translations.literal: Zhongkan said: "I have worried about this for a long time. What plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan said, "I have worried about this a long time. What do you advise?"

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「孝伯疾惡深至，君宜潛與之約，興晉陽之甲以除君側之惡，東西齊舉，玄雖不肖，願帥荊、楚豪傑，荷戈先驅，此桓、文之勳也。」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Xiao Bo's hatred runs very deep. You should secretly arrange with him to raise the armies of Jinyang to remove the evil at the emperor's side. If east and west rise together, though I am unworthy, I would lead the heroes of Jing and Chu, spear in hand, as vanguard—this would be an achievement like Duke Huan's and Duke Wen's."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "Wang Gong hates them to the bone. Secretly join him, raise Jinyang's armies to purge the court, and strike together east and west. Though I am unworthy, I will lead Jing and Chu with spear in hand—a feat worthy of Duke Huan or Duke Wen."

sentences.zh: 仲堪心然之，乃外結雍州荊史郗恢，內與從兄南蠻校尉覬、南郡相陳留江績謀之。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was inwardly persuaded; he then allied outwardly with Yingzhou Inspector Xi Hui of Yongzhou, and inwardly plotted with his cousin the Colonel of Southern Man Kai and Nanjun Chancellor Jiang Ji of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan agreed; he reached out to Yingzhou Inspector Xi Hui and plotted inwardly with his cousin Colonel of Southern Man Yin Kai and Nanjun Chancellor Jiang Ji of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 覬曰：「人臣各守職分，朝廷是非，豈籓屏之所制也！

translations.literal: Kai said: "As ministers we each keep to our duties. How can a frontier screen control right and wrong at court!
translations.idiomatic: Kai said, "Ministers keep to their posts—how can a frontier governor judge the court's right and wrong!

sentences.zh: 晉陽之事，不敢預聞。」

translations.literal: I dare not hear of any Jinyang affair."
translations.idiomatic: I will have no part in any Jinyang rising."

sentences.zh: 仲堪固邀之，覬怒曰：「吾進不敢同，退不敢異。」

translations.literal: Zhongkan pressed him insistently; Kai angrily said: "If I advance I dare not join you; if I retreat I dare not differ from you."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongkan pressed him, Kai angrily said, "If I go forward I dare not join you; if I hold back I dare not oppose you."

sentences.zh: 績亦極言其不可。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji also spoke at length that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji also argued at length against it.

sentences.zh: 覬恐績及禍，於坐和解之。

translations.literal: Kai feared Ji would come to harm and at the gathering made peace between them.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, fearing harm to Ji, reconciled them at the meeting.

sentences.zh: 績曰：「大丈夫何至以死相脅邪？

translations.literal: Ji said: "Why would a true man threaten another with death?
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Would a true man threaten another with death?

sentences.zh: 江仲元行年六十，但未獲死所耳！」

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan is sixty years old—he simply has not yet found the place to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan is sixty—I simply have not yet found where to die!"

sentences.zh: 仲堪憚其堅正，以楊佺期代之。

translations.literal: Zhongkan feared his firm integrity and replaced him with Yang Quanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan, awed by his integrity, replaced him with Yang Quanqi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，征績為御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the court heard of this, Ji was summoned to be Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard of it and summoned Ji to be Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 覬遂稱疾發，辭位。

translations.literal: Kai then claimed a sudden illness and resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Kai then feigned sudden illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 仲堪往省之，謂覬曰：「兄病殊為可憂。」

translations.literal: Zhongkan went to visit him and said to Kai: "Brother, your illness is truly worrisome."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan visited him and said, "Brother, your illness is deeply worrying."

sentences.zh: 覬曰：「我病不過身死，汝病乃當滅門。

translations.literal: Kai said: "My illness is no more than death of the body; your illness will destroy your whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai said, "My illness is only my own death; yours will destroy your whole clan.

sentences.zh: 宜深自愛，勿以我為念！」

translations.literal: Take good care of yourself; do not think of me!"
translations.idiomatic: Guard yourself well—do not think of me!"

sentences.zh: 郗恢亦不肯從。

translations.literal: Xi Hui also refused to join.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Hui also refused.

sentences.zh: 仲堪疑未決，會王恭使至，仲堪許之，恭大喜。

translations.literal: Zhongkan still hesitated without decision; when Wang Gong's envoy arrived, Zhongkan agreed; Gong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan still wavered; when Wang Gong's envoy arrived he consented, and Gong rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，恭上表罪狀國寶，舉兵討之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Gong submitted a memorial listing Guobao's crimes and raised troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Wang Gong memorialized Guobao's crimes and took up arms against him.

sentences.zh: 初，孝武帝委任王珣，及帝暴崩，不及受顧命，珣一旦失勢，循默而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Xiaowu had entrusted Wang Xun; when the emperor died suddenly without Xun receiving a final charge, Xun lost power at once and kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu had favored Wang Xun; when the emperor died suddenly without naming Xun in his final charge, Xun lost influence and kept quiet.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，王恭表至，外戒嚴嚴，道子問珣曰：「二籓作逆，卿知之乎？」

translations.literal: On dingchou, Wang Gong's memorial arrived; outer defenses were strictly manned; Daozi asked Xun: "The two fiefs are in rebellion—did you know of it?"
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Gong's memorial arrived and outer defenses were tightened; Daozi asked Xun, "The two frontier lords are in revolt—did you know?"

sentences.zh: 珣曰：「朝政得失，珣弗之預，王、殷作難，何由可知！」

translations.literal: Xun said: "I had no part in the rights and wrongs of court governance; how could I know that Wang and Yin were raising trouble!"
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "I had no hand in court affairs—how could I know Wang and Yin were rising?"

sentences.zh: 王國寶惶懼，不知所為，遣數百人戍竹裡，夜遇風雨，各散歸。

translations.literal: Guobao was frightened and did not know what to do; he sent several hundred men to garrison Zhuli; at night they met wind and rain and each scattered home.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao panicked; he sent hundreds to garrison Zhuli, but a night storm scattered them home.

sentences.zh: 王緒說國寶矯相王之命召王珣、車胤殺之，以除時望，因挾君相發兵以討二籓。

translations.literal: Wang Xu urged Guobao to forge the Prince's orders to summon Wang Xun and Che Yin and kill them, removing those the times looked to, then seize emperor and regent to raise troops against the two fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xu urged Guobao to forge Daozi's orders, summon Wang Xun and Che Yin and kill them, then seize emperor and regent to attack the two fiefs.

sentences.zh: 國寶許之。

translations.literal: Guobao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao agreed.

sentences.zh: 珣、胤至，國寶不敢害，更問計於珣。

translations.literal: When Xun and Yin arrived, Guobao did not dare harm them and instead asked Xun for advice.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun and Yin arrived, Guobao dared not kill them and asked Xun's counsel.

sentences.zh: 珣曰：「王、殷與卿素無深怨，所競不過勢利之間耳。」

translations.literal: Xun said: "Wang and Yin have never borne you deep grudges; what you compete over is nothing more than power and profit."
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "Wang and Yin bear you no deep grudge—you merely compete for power and profit."

sentences.zh: 國寶曰；

translations.literal: Guobao said;
translations.idiomatic: Guobao said,

sentences.zh: 「將曹爽我乎？」

translations.literal: "Will they treat me like Cao Shuang?"
translations.idiomatic: "Will they do to me what was done to Cao Shuang?"

sentences.zh: 珣曰：「是何言歟！
