translations.literal: Xun said: "What talk is this!
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "What kind of talk is that!

sentences.zh: 卿寧有爽之罪，王孝伯豈宣帝之儔邪？」

translations.literal: You surely have not Cao Shuang's crimes—is Wang Xiaobo a match for Emperor Xuan of Jin?"
translations.idiomatic: You are no Cao Shuang—is Wang Gong another Sima Yi?"

sentences.zh: 又問計於胤，胤曰：「昔桓公圍壽陽，彌時乃克。

translations.literal: He also asked Yin for advice; Yin said: "Formerly Duke Huan besieged Shouyang and took it only after a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Yin; Yin said, "When Duke Huan besieged Shouyang, it took a long time to fall.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷遣軍，恭必城守。

translations.literal: Now if the court sends armies, Gong is sure to hold his city.
translations.idiomatic: If the court sends troops now, Gong will hold his city.

sentences.zh: 若京口未拔而上流奄至，君將何以待之？」

translations.literal: If Jingkou is not taken before forces from upstream arrive suddenly, how will you cope?"
translations.idiomatic: If Jingkou is not taken before upstream armies arrive, what will you do?"

sentences.zh: 國寶尤懼，遂上疏解職，詣闕待罪。

translations.literal: Guobao was all the more afraid; he submitted a memorial resigning office and went to the palace to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao was terrified; he resigned and went to the palace to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，詐稱詔復其本官。

translations.literal: He soon regretted it and falsely claimed an edict restoring him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted it and falsely claimed an edict restoring his office.

sentences.zh: 道子暗懦，欲求姑息，乃委罪國寶，遣縹騎咨議參軍譙王尚之收國寶付廷尉。

translations.literal: Daozi was dim and weak and wished to reach a compromise; he therefore laid blame on Guobao and sent the pale-robed rider Consultant Wang Shangzhi to seize Guobao and hand him to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi, weak and seeking compromise, blamed Guobao and sent Consultant Wang Shangzhi to seize him for the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 尚之，恬之子也。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was the son of Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was the son of Wang Tian.

sentences.zh: 甲申，賜國寶死，斬緒於市，遣使詣恭，深謝愆失；

translations.literal: On jiashen, Guobao was sentenced to death; Xu was executed in the marketplace; envoys were sent to Gong with deep apologies for the transgressions;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Guobao was executed and Xu beheaded in the market; envoys apologized deeply to Gong;

sentences.zh: 恭乃罷兵還京口。

translations.literal: Gong then stood down his troops and returned to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong then disbanded and returned to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 國寶兄侍中愷、驃騎司馬愉並請解職；

translations.literal: Guobao's elder brothers, Attendant-in-Ordinary Kai and Chief of Staff to the Cavalry-in-Chief Yu, both requested to resign;
translations.idiomatic: Guobao's half-brothers Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Kai and Cavalry Chief of Staff Wang Yu both asked to resign;

sentences.zh: 道子以愷、愉與國寶異母，又素不協，皆釋不問。

translations.literal: Daozi, because Kai and Yu were Guobao's half-brothers and had long been on bad terms with him, released them without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi, noting they were Guobao's half-brothers and long estranged from him, released them without punishment.

sentences.zh: 戊子，大赦。

translations.literal: On wuzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪雖許王恭，猶豫不敢下；

translations.literal: Yin Zhongkan had agreed to Wang Gong but hesitated and did not dare advance;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan had promised Wang Gong but hesitated to move;

sentences.zh: 聞國寶等死，乃始抗表舉兵，遣楊佺期屯巴陵。

translations.literal: On hearing that Guobao and the others were dead, he only then submitted a defiant memorial and raised troops, sending Yang Quanqi to garrison Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Guobao's death did he submit a defiant memorial, raise troops, and send Yang Quanqi to Baling.

sentences.zh: 道子以書止之，仲堪乃還。

translations.literal: Daozi stopped him by letter; Zhongkan then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi checked him by letter and Zhongkan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會稽世子元顯，年十六，有雋才，為侍中，說道子以王、殷終必為患，請潛為之備。

translations.literal: Kuaiji heir Yuanxian, aged sixteen, had brilliant talent; as Attendant-in-Ordinary he told Daozi that Wang and Yin would ultimately be a threat and asked to prepare against them secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji heir Sima Yuanxian, sixteen and brilliant, warned Daozi that Wang and Yin would become a lasting threat and asked to prepare secretly.

sentences.zh: 道子乃拜元顯征虜將軍，以其衛府及徐州文武悉配之。

translations.literal: Daozi then made Yuanxian General Who Punishes Barbarians and assigned to him his guard office and all Xuzhou civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi made Yuanxian General Who Punishes Barbarians and gave him his guard staff and all Xuzhou officials.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪以軍食不給，命東平公儀去鄴，徙屯巨鹿，積租楊城。

translations.literal: Wei King Gui, because army provisions were insufficient, ordered the Duke of Dongping, Yi, to leave Ye, move camp to Julu, and gather rents at Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei King Tuoba Gui, short of provisions, ordered Duke of Dongping Tuoba Yi to leave Ye, camp at Julu, and levy grain at Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 慕容詳出步卒六千人，伺間襲魏諸屯；

translations.literal: Murong Xiang sent out six thousand foot soldiers to seize an opportunity and raid Wei's camps;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xiang sent six thousand foot to raid Wei camps when chance offered;

sentences.zh: 珪擊破之，斬首五千，生擒七百人，皆縱之。

translations.literal: Gui routed them, beheaded five thousand, captured seven hundred alive, and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui routed them, killed five thousand, captured seven hundred, and released them all.

sentences.zh: 初，張掖盧水胡沮渠羅仇，匈奴沮渠王之後也，世為部帥。

translations.literal: Earlier, Juqu Luogou of the Lushui Hu of Zhangye was a descendant of the Xiongnu King Juqu; for generations his family had been chieftains of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Luogou of the Lushui Hu in Zhangye was descended from the Xiongnu Juqu kings and had led his tribe for generations.

sentences.zh: 涼王光以羅仇為尚書，從光伐西秦。

translations.literal: Liang King Guang made Luogou Director of the Imperial Secretariat and took him along to attack Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang King Lü Guang made Luogou a Director of the Secretariat and took him to attack Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 及呂延敗死，羅仇弟三河太守麴粥謂羅仇曰：「主上荒耄信讒，今軍敗將死，正其猜忌智勇之時也。

translations.literal: When Lü Yan was defeated and killed, Luogou's younger brother Qu Mi, Administrator of Sanhe, said to Luogou: "Our lord is senile and trusts slander; now that the army is defeated and the general dead, this is precisely when he will grow suspicious of the wise and brave.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Yan was defeated and killed, Luogou's brother Qu Mi, Administrator of Sanhe, said, "Our lord is old, muddled, and trusts slander; with the army broken and the general dead, he will now turn on the able.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟必不見容，與其死之無名，不若勒兵向西平。

translations.literal: Our brothers will surely not be tolerated; rather than die without renown, better to muster troops toward Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: We will not be spared; better to die with purpose—muster troops toward Xiping.

sentences.zh: 出苕藋，奮臂一呼，涼州不足定也。」

translations.literal: Once we reach Tiaomiao and raise an arm with one shout, Liangzhou will be easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Reach Tiaomiao, raise one cry, and Liangzhou is ours."

sentences.zh: 羅仇曰；

translations.literal: Luogou said;
translations.idiomatic: Luogou said,

sentences.zh: 「誠如汝言。

translations.literal: "It is truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 然吾家世以忠孝著於西土，寧使人負我，我不忍負人也。」

translations.literal: Yet our family for generations has been known for loyalty and filial piety in the western lands; I would rather be wronged by others than wrong others myself."
translations.idiomatic: Yet our house has been known for loyalty in the west; I would rather be wronged than wrong others."

sentences.zh: 光果聽讒，以敗軍之罪殺羅仇及麴粥。

translations.literal: Guang indeed listened to slander and executed Luogou and Qu Mi on the charge of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang listened to slander and executed Luogou and Qu Mi for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 羅仇弟子蒙遜，雄傑有策略，涉獵書史，以羅仇、麴粥之喪歸葬；

translations.literal: Luogou's nephew Mengsun was a heroic strategist who ranged widely in books and history; he returned to bury Luogou and Qu Mi;
translations.idiomatic: Luogou's nephew Juqu Mengsun, a bold strategist versed in history, returned to bury Luogou and Qu Mi;

sentences.zh: 諸部多其族姻，會葬者凡萬餘人。

translations.literal: Many tribes were related to his clan; more than ten thousand gathered for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Many tribes were kin; more than ten thousand attended the funeral.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜哭謂眾曰：「呂王昏荒無道，多殺不辜。

translations.literal: Mengsun wept and said to the crowd: "King Lü is muddled and lawless, killing many innocents.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun wept and told the crowd, "King Lü is lawless and kills the innocent.

sentences.zh: 吾之上世，虎視河西，今欲與諸部雪二父之恥，復上世之業，何如？」

translations.literal: My ancestors once looked down on Hexi from power; now I wish to join the tribes to avenge our two fathers and restore our forefathers' enterprise—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: My ancestors once ruled Hexi; will you join me to avenge our fathers and restore that legacy?"

sentences.zh: 眾咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: All cried ten thousand years of life.
translations.idiomatic: All shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 遂結盟起兵，攻涼臨松郡，拔之，屯據金山。

translations.literal: They then formed an alliance and rose in arms, attacked Liang's Linsong commandery, took it, and encamped at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: They allied, rose in arms, took Liang's Linsong commandery, and encamped at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 司徒左長史王廞，導之孫也，以母喪居吳。

translations.literal: Left Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister of Works Wang Yin, grandson of Wang Dao, was living in Wu during mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin, left chief clerk to the Grand Minister of Works and grandson of Wang Dao, was mourning his mother in Wu.

sentences.zh: 王恭之討王國寶也，版廞行吳國內史，使起兵於東方。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong attacked Wang Guobao, he issued a commission appointing Yin Acting Administrator of Wu and ordered him to raise troops in the east.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gong moved against Guobao, he commissioned Wang Yin Acting Administrator of Wu to raise troops in the east.

sentences.zh: 廞使前吳國內史虞嘯等入吳興、義興召募兵眾，赴者萬計。

translations.literal: Yin sent the former Administrator Yu Xiao and others into Wuxing and Yixing to recruit soldiers; those who came numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent former Administrator Yu Xiao and others into Wuxing and Yixing to recruit; tens of thousands answered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，國寶死，恭罷兵，符珪去職，反喪服。

translations.literal: Before long Guobao died, Gong stood down; Yin left office and resumed mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guobao was dead, Gong stood down, and Yin left office to resume mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 廞以起兵之際，誅異己者頗多，勢不得止，遂大怒，不承恭命，使其子泰將兵伐恭，箋於會稽王道子，稱恭罪惡；

translations.literal: Because at the time of raising troops he had killed many who differed from him and could not stop, Yin grew furious, refused Gong's orders, sent his son Tai with troops to attack Gong, and wrote to Kuaiji Prince Daozi listing Gong's crimes;
translations.idiomatic: Having killed many rivals when he mobilized, Yin could not stop; he defied Gong, sent his son Tai against him, and wrote Daozi denouncing Gong;

sentences.zh: 道子以其箋送恭，五月，恭遣司馬劉牢之帥五千人擊泰，斬之。

translations.literal: Daozi forwarded his letter to Gong; in the fifth month, Gong sent Marshal Liu Laozhi with five thousand men to attack Tai and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi forwarded the letter to Gong; in the fifth month Gong sent Liu Laozhi with five thousand men, killed Tai, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 又與廞戰於曲阿，眾潰，廞單騎走，不知所在。

translations.literal: He also fought Yin at Qu'a; the host scattered; Yin fled alone on horseback and his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He then fought Yin at Qu'a; Yin's force collapsed; Yin fled alone and vanished.

sentences.zh: 收虞嘯父下廷尉，以其祖潭有功，免為庶人。

translations.literal: Yu Xiao's father was seized and sent to the Court of Judicial Review; because his grandfather Tan had merit, he was pardoned and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiao's father was sent to the Court of Judicial Review; because his grandfather Tan had served well, he was pardoned to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 燕庫辱官驥入中山，與開封公詳相攻。

translations.literal: Yan's Kuru official Ji entered Zhongshan and fought the Duke of Kaifeng, Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan's Kuru official Ji entered Zhongshan and clashed with Duke of Kaifeng Murong Xiang.

sentences.zh: 詳殺驥，盡滅庫辱官氏；

translations.literal: Xiang killed Ji and exterminated the Kuru official clan;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xiang killed Ji and wiped out the Kuru official clan;

sentences.zh: 又殺中山尹苻謨，夷其族。

translations.literal: He also killed Zhongshan Prefect Fu Mo and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Zhongshan Prefect Fu Mo and exterminated his family.

sentences.zh: 中山城無定主，民恐魏兵乘之，男女結盟，人自為戰。

translations.literal: Zhongshan had no settled ruler; the people feared Wei would seize the chance; men and women swore oaths and each fought for himself.
translations.idiomatic: With no stable ruler in Zhongshan, the people feared Wei would strike; families swore oaths and fought on their own.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏王珪罷中山之圍，就谷河間，督諸郡義租。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Wei King Gui lifted the siege of Zhongshan, moved to forage in Hejian, and supervised righteous levies in the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Tuoba Gui lifted the Zhongshan siege, foraged in Hejian, and collected emergency grain across the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以東平公儀為驃騎大將軍、都督中外諸軍事、兗、豫、雍、荊、徐、揚六州牧、左丞相，封衛王。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Duke of Dongping, Yi, was made Cavalry-in-Chief, Commander-in-Chief of All Forces, Governor of Yan, Yu, Yong, Jing, Xu, and Yang, Left Chancellor, and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Tuoba Yi was made Cavalry-in-Chief, supreme commander, governor of six provinces, Left Chancellor, and Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 慕容詳自謂能卻魏兵，威德已振，乃即皇帝位，改元建始，置百官。

translations.literal: Murong Xiang believed himself able to repel Wei and that his prestige had risen; he thereupon assumed the imperial title, changed the era name to Jianshi, and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xiang, confident he could beat Wei, declared himself emperor, adopted the era Jianshi, and set up a court.

sentences.zh: 以新平公可足渾潭為車騎大將軍、尚書令，殺拓跋觚以固眾心。

translations.literal: He made the Duke of Xinping, Kezuhun Tan, Cavalry-in-Chief and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and killed Tuoba Gu to steady the hearts of the host.
translations.idiomatic: He made Kezuhun Tan Cavalry-in-Chief and Director of the Secretariat and killed the Wei hostage Tuoba Gu to win loyalty.

sentences.zh: 鄴中官屬勸范陽王德稱尊號，會有自龍城來者，知燕主寶猶存，乃止。

translations.literal: Officials in Ye urged the Prince of Fanyang, De, to take the imperial title; when someone arrived from Longcheng reporting that Yan ruler Bao still lived, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ye officials urged Prince of Fanyang Murong De to declare himself emperor; news from Longcheng that Murong Bao still lived stopped them.

sentences.zh: 涼王光遣太原公纂將兵擊沮渠蒙遜忽谷，破之。

translations.literal: Liang King Guang sent the Prince of Taiyuan, Zuan, with troops to attack Juqu Mengsun at Hugu and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent Prince of Taiyuan Lü Zuan to attack Juqu Mengsun at Hugu and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜逃入山中。

translations.literal: Mengsun fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜從兄男成為涼將軍，聞蒙遜起兵，亦合眾數千屯樂涫。

translations.literal: Mengsun's cousin Nancheng, a Liang general, heard Mengsun had risen and also gathered several thousand men at Yueguan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun's cousin Juqu Nancheng, a Liang general, heard of the revolt and gathered thousands at Yueguan.

sentences.zh: 酒泉太守壘澄討男成，兵敗，澄死。

translations.literal: Jiuquan Administrator Lei Cheng attacked Nancheng; his army was defeated and Cheng died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuquan Administrator Lei Cheng attacked Nancheng, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 男成進攻建康，遣使說建康太守段業曰：「呂氏政衰，權臣擅命，刑殺無常，人無容處。

translations.literal: Nancheng advanced on Jiankang and sent envoys to persuade Jiankang Administrator Duan Ye, saying: "The Lü house is in decline; powerful ministers act at will; punishments and killings are arbitrary and people have nowhere to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng marched on Jiankang and urged Administrator Duan Ye, "The Lü regime is failing; ministers rule by force; killings are random and no one is safe.

sentences.zh: 一州之地，叛者相望，瓦解之形，昭然在目，百姓嗷然無所依附。

translations.literal: Rebellion stretches across the province; collapse is plain to see; the people cry out with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels fill the province; collapse is obvious; the people have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 府君奈何以蓋世之才，欲立忠於垂亡之國！

translations.literal: My lord, with talent fit for the age, why seek loyalty in a dying state!
translations.idiomatic: My lord, with your gifts, why die for a doomed state!

sentences.zh: 男成等既唱大義，欲屈府君撫臨鄙州，使塗炭之餘，蒙來蘇之惠，何如？」

translations.literal: We have raised the righteous banner and ask you to rule this land so the suffering may know relief—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: We ask you to lead this region and bring the people back to life—will you accept?"

sentences.zh: 業不從。

translations.literal: Ye did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Ye refused.

sentences.zh: 相持二旬，外救不至，郡人高逵、史惠等勸業從男成之請。

translations.literal: After twenty days of stalemate with no relief, the commandery men Gao Kui and Shi Hui urged Ye to accept Nancheng's request.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty days without relief, Gao Kui and Shi Hui urged Ye to accept.

sentences.zh: 業素與涼侍中房晷、僕射王詳不平，懼不自安，乃許之。

translations.literal: Ye had long been at odds with Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary Fang Chao and Vice Director Wang Xiang; fearing for himself, he consented.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, feuding with Fang Chao and Wang Xiang and fearing for his safety, agreed.

sentences.zh: 男成等推業為大都督、龍驤大將軍、涼州牧、建康公，改元神璽。

translations.literal: Nancheng and the others made Ye Grand Commander, General of the Dragon Cavalry, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiankang, and changed the era name to Shenxi.
translations.idiomatic: They made Ye Grand Commander, Dragon Cavalry General, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiankang, with era Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 以男成為輔國將軍，委以軍國之任。

translations.literal: Nancheng was made General Who Supports the State and entrusted with military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng was made General Who Supports the State with full military authority.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜帥眾歸業，業以蒙遜為鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Mengsun led his host to join Ye; Ye made Mengsun General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun joined Ye with his army; Ye made him General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 光命太原公纂將兵討業，不克。

translations.literal: Guang ordered the Prince of Taiyuan, Zuan, with troops to attack Ye but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent Lü Zuan against Ye but failed to take him.

sentences.zh: 六月，西秦王乾歸征河州刺史彭奚念為鎮衛將軍；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Western Qin ruler Qiangui appointed Peng Xinian of Hezhou as General Who Guards the Realm;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Western Qin ruler Qifu Qiangui made Peng Xinian of Hezhou General Who Guards the Realm;

sentences.zh: 以鎮西將軍屋弘破光為河州牧；

translations.literal: He made General Who Guards the West Wuyu Hong, who had defeated Guang, Governor of Hezhou;
translations.idiomatic: He made Wuyu Hong, who had defeated Guang, Governor of Hezhou;

sentences.zh: 定州刺史翟瑁為興晉太守，鎮枹罕。

translations.literal: He made Zhai Wei of Dingzhou Xingjin Administrator and garrisoned Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhai Wei Xingjin Administrator and stationed him at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，慕容詳殺可足渾潭。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Murong Xiang killed Kezuhun Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Murong Xiang killed Kezuhun Tan.

sentences.zh: 詳嗜酒奢浮，不恤士民，刑殺無度，所誅王公以下五百餘人，群下離心。

translations.literal: Xiang was addicted to wine and lived in extravagance; he did not care for soldiers or people; punishments and killings were boundless; more than five hundred from princes and dukes downward were executed; subordinates lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang drank heavily, lived lavishly, ignored soldiers and people, and executed more than five hundred from princes down; his followers turned against him.

sentences.zh: 城中饑窘，詳不聽民出采穭，死者相枕，舉城皆謀迎趙王麟。

translations.literal: Famine gripped the city; Xiang would not let the people go out to gather wild grain; the dead lay piled; the whole city plotted to welcome Prince Zhao Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Starvation gripped the city; Xiang forbade foraging; corpses piled up; the city plotted to welcome Prince Zhao Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 詳遣輔國將軍張驤帥五千餘人督租於常山，麟自丁零入驤軍，潛襲中山，城門不閉，執詳，斬之。

translations.literal: Xiang sent General Who Supports the State Zhang Yang with more than five thousand men to supervise rent collection in Changshan; Lin entered Yang's army from the Dingling and secretly struck Zhongshan; the gates were not closed; they seized Xiang and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang sent Zhang Yang with five thousand to levy grain in Changshan; Murong Lin infiltrated Yang's force from Dingling, seized Zhongshan with gates open, captured Xiang, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 麟遂稱尊號，聽人四出采穭。

translations.literal: Lin then assumed the imperial title and allowed people to go out in all directions to gather wild grain.
translations.idiomatic: Lin declared himself emperor and let the people forage freely.

sentences.zh: 人既飽，求與魏戰。

translations.literal: Once the people were fed, they asked to fight Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Once fed, they demanded battle with Wei.

sentences.zh: 麟不從，稍復窮餒。

translations.literal: Lin did not agree; they soon grew hungry again.
translations.idiomatic: Lin refused; hunger returned.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪軍魯口，遣長孫肥帥騎七千襲中山，入其郛；

translations.literal: Wei King Gui was at Lukou; he sent Zhangsun Fei with seven thousand horsemen in a surprise attack on Zhongshan; they entered the outer wall;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui camped at Lukou and sent Zhangsun Fei with seven thousand horse to raid Zhongshan and enter the outer city;

sentences.zh: 麟進至泒水，為魏所敗而還。

translations.literal: Lin advanced to the Gushui River, was defeated by Wei, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin advanced to the Gushui, was beaten by Wei, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙寅朔，魏王珪徙軍常山之九門。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of the month, bingyin, Wei King Gui moved his army to Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingyin, the new moon, Tuoba Gui moved to Jiumen in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 軍中大疫，人畜多死，將士皆思歸。

translations.literal: Plague broke out in the army; many men and livestock died; officers and soldiers all wished to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Plague ravaged the army; men and livestock died in masses; the troops wanted to go home.

sentences.zh: 珪問疫於諸將，對曰：「在者才什四、五。」

translations.literal: Gui asked the generals about the plague; they replied: "Of those who remain, only four or five tenths."
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui asked his generals about the plague; they said, "Only four or five tenths remain."

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「此固天命，將若之何？

translations.literal: Gui said: "This is truly Heaven's mandate—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This is Heaven's will—what can we do?

sentences.zh: 四海之民，皆可為國，在吾所以御之耳，何患無民！」

translations.literal: The people of the four seas may all become a state; it lies in how I govern them—why worry about lacking people!"
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven can become my people—it depends on how I rule them—why fear a shortage of men!"

sentences.zh: 群臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: The ministers then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers fell silent.

sentences.zh: 遣撫軍大將軍略陽公遵襲中山，入其郛而還。

translations.literal: He sent the Pacifying Army Grand General, the Duke of Lueyang, Zun, in a surprise attack on Zhongshan; they entered the outer wall and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Duke of Lueyang Tuoba Zun to raid Zhongshan, enter the outer wall, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 燕以遼西王農為都督中外諸軍事、大司馬、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Yan made the Prince of Liaoxi, Nong, Commander-in-Chief of All Forces, Grand Marshal, and Recorder of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan made Prince of Liaoxi Murong Nong supreme commander, Grand Marshal, and Recorder of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 涼散騎常侍、太常西平郭黁，善天文數術，國人信重之。

translations.literal: Liang Palace Attendant Guo Fen of Xiping, skilled in astronomy and numerology, was trusted and respected by the people of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang Palace Attendant Guo Fen of Xiping, expert in astronomy and divination, was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 會熒惑守東井，黁謂僕射王詳曰：「涼之分野，將有大兵。

translations.literal: When Mars stayed in the Eastern Well constellation, Fen said to Vice Director Wang Xiang: "This is Liang's allotted region—great war is coming.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars lodged in the Eastern Well, Fen told Wang Xiang, "Liang's fate is under attack—great war approaches.

sentences.zh: 主上老病，太子闇弱，太原公凶悍。

translations.literal: The ruler is old and ill; the crown prince is dim and weak; the Prince of Taiyuan is fierce and brutal.
translations.idiomatic: The king is old and sick; the heir is weak; Prince of Taiyuan Lü Zuan is savage.

sentences.zh: 一旦不諱，禍亂必起。

translations.literal: Once he passes away, turmoil is sure to rise.
translations.idiomatic: When he dies, chaos will follow.

sentences.zh: 吾二人久居內要，彼常切齒，將為誅首矣。

translations.literal: We two have long held inner power—they grind their teeth at us and will make us the first heads to fall.
translations.idiomatic: We have long held inner power—they hate us and will kill us first.

sentences.zh: 田胡王乞基部落最強，二苑之人，多其舊眾。

translations.literal: Tianhu King Qi Ji's tribe is strongest; many in the two parks are his old followers.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhu King Qi Ji's tribe is strongest; many in the two parks follow him.

sentences.zh: 吾欲與公舉大事，推乞基為主，二苑之眾，盡我有也。

translations.literal: I wish to join you in a great enterprise, set up Qi Ji as leader, and the people of the two parks will all be ours.
translations.idiomatic: Let us raise a revolt, make Qi Ji leader, and the two parks will be ours.

sentences.zh: 得城之後，徐更議之。」

translations.literal: After we take the city, we can discuss matters further."
translations.idiomatic: Once we hold the city, we can decide what comes next."

sentences.zh: 詳從之。

translations.literal: Xiang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang agreed.

sentences.zh: 黁夜以二苑之眾燒洪範門，使詳為內應；

translations.literal: By night Fen led the people of the two parks to burn the Hongfan Gate, with Xiang as inner ally;
translations.idiomatic: Fen led the two parks by night to burn the Hongfan Gate, with Xiang as inside contact;

sentences.zh: 事洩，詳被誅，黁遂據東苑以叛。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; Xiang was executed; Fen then seized the Eastern Park and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked; Xiang was killed; Fen seized the Eastern Park and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 民間皆言聖人起兵，事無不成，從之者甚眾。

translations.literal: Among the people all said a sage had risen in arms and nothing would fail; very many followed.
translations.idiomatic: People said a sage had risen and success was assured; multitudes joined.

sentences.zh: 涼王光召太原公纂使討黁。

translations.literal: Liang King Guang summoned the Prince of Taiyuan, Zuan, to attack Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang summoned Lü Zuan to suppress Fen.

sentences.zh: 纂將還，諸將皆曰：「段業必躡軍後，宜潛師夜發。」

translations.literal: As Zuan was about to return, the generals all said: "Duan Ye is sure to follow on our rear—we should move the army secretly by night."
translations.idiomatic: As Zuan prepared to withdraw, his generals said, "Duan Ye will pursue—we should march by night."

sentences.zh: 纂曰：「業無雄才，恁城自守；

translations.literal: Zuan said: "Ye has no heroic talent and relies on his walls alone;
translations.idiomatic: Zuan said, "Ye lacks ability and will only hold his walls;

sentences.zh: 若潛師夜去，適足張其氣勢耳。」

translations.literal: If we slip away by night, we would only inflate his morale."
translations.idiomatic: A secret night march would only boost his confidence."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使告業曰：「郭黁作亂，吾今還都；

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to tell Ye: "Guo Fen has rebelled; I am returning to the capital now;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ye word, "Guo Fen has rebelled; I am returning to the capital;

sentences.zh: 卿能決者，可早出戰。」

translations.literal: If you dare decide, you may sally out early to fight."
translations.idiomatic: if you dare, come out and fight."

sentences.zh: 於是引還。

translations.literal: He then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched back.

sentences.zh: 業不敢出。

translations.literal: Ye did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: Ye dared not sally.

sentences.zh: 纂司馬楊統謂其從兄桓曰：「郭黁舉事，必不虛發。

translations.literal: Zuan's marshal Yang Tong said to his cousin Huan: "Guo Fen's rising is surely no empty move.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's marshal Yang Tong told his cousin Huan, "Guo Fen's revolt is no bluff.

sentences.zh: 吾欲殺纂，推兄為主，西襲呂弘，據張掖，號令諸郡，此千載一時也。」

translations.literal: I wish to kill Zuan, set you up as leader, strike west at Lü Hong, seize Zhangye, and command the commanderies—this is a chance of a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: I want to kill Zuan, make you leader, strike Lü Hong in the west, seize Zhangye, and command the region—a once-in-a-thousand-years chance."

sentences.zh: 桓怒曰：「吾為呂氏臣，安享其祿，危不能救，豈可復增其難乎？

translations.literal: Huan angrily said: "I am a minister of the Lü house and enjoy its salary; though I cannot save it in crisis, how can I add to its troubles?
translations.idiomatic: Huan angrily replied, "I serve the Lü house and eat its pay; though I cannot save it in crisis, how can I make it worse?

sentences.zh: 呂氏若亡，吾為弘演矣！」

translations.literal: If the Lü house falls, I shall be Hong Yan!"
translations.idiomatic: If the Lü fall, I will be another Hong Yan!"

sentences.zh: 統至番禾，遂叛歸黁。

translations.literal: Tong reached Fanhe and then rebelled and went over to Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Tong reached Fanhe and defected to Fen.

sentences.zh: 弘，纂之弟也。

translations.literal: Hong was Zuan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong was Zuan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 纂與西安太守石元良共擊黁，大破之，乃得入姑臧。

translations.literal: Zuan with Xi'an Administrator Shi Yuanliang jointly attacked Fen and inflicted a great defeat; only then could he enter Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan and Xi'an Administrator Shi Yuanliang crushed Fen and at last entered Guzang.

sentences.zh: 黁得光孫八人於東苑，及敗而恚，悉投於鋒上，枝分節解，飲其血以盟眾，眾皆掩目。

translations.literal: Fen had taken eight of Guang's grandsons in the Eastern Park; when defeated he was enraged and impaled them all on blades, limb from limb, drank their blood to swear the host, and all covered their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Fen had seized eight of Guang's grandsons in the Eastern Park; defeated, he dismembered them on spears, drank their blood to swear his men, and all looked away.

sentences.zh: 涼人張捷、宋生等招集戎、夏三千人，反於休屠城，與黁共推涼後將軍楊軌為盟主。

translations.literal: Liang men Zhang Jie, Song Sheng, and others gathered three thousand Rong and Xia at Xiutu city and rebelled, joining Fen in making the Later Liang Rear General Yang Gui covenant leader.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie, Song Sheng, and others raised three thousand Rong and Xia at Xiutu and with Fen made Rear General Yang Gui their covenant leader.

sentences.zh: 軌，略陽氐也。

translations.literal: Gui was Di of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui was Lueyang Di.

sentences.zh: 將軍程肇諫曰：「卿棄龍頭而從蛇尾，非計也。」

translations.literal: General Cheng Zhao remonstrated, saying: "You abandon the dragon's head to follow the snake's tail—this is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: General Cheng Zhao warned, "You leave the dragon's head to follow the snake's tail—bad strategy."

sentences.zh: 軌不從，自稱大將軍、涼州牧、西平公。

translations.literal: Gui did not agree and styled himself Grand General, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Gui refused and styled himself Grand General, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 纂擊破黁將王斐於城西，黁兵勢漸衰，遣使請救於禿髮烏孤。

translations.literal: Zuan defeated Fen's general Wang Fei west of the city; Fen's army gradually weakened and he sent envoys asking Tufa Wugu for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan beat Fen's general Wang Fei west of the city; Fen weakened and asked Tufa Wugu for aid.

sentences.zh: 九月，烏孤使其弟驃騎將軍利鹿孤帥騎兵五千赴之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wugu sent his younger brother, Cavalry-in-Chief Lilugu, with five thousand horsemen to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wugu sent his brother Lilugu with five thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 秦太后蛇氏卒。

translations.literal: Qin Empress Dowager Lady She died.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin Empress Dowager Lady She died.

sentences.zh: 秦主興哀毀過禮，不親庶政。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Xing mourned beyond the rites and did not attend to ordinary governance.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Yao Xing mourned excessively and neglected government.

sentences.zh: 群臣請依漢、魏故事，即葬即吉。

translations.literal: The ministers asked to follow Han and Wei precedent—burial and then return to normal mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers asked to follow Han and Wei custom and resume rule after burial.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎李嵩上疏曰：「孝治天下，先王之高事也。

translations.literal: Secretary Lang Li Song submitted a memorial saying: "Filial piety governs the world—it is the high affair of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Li Song memorialized, "Filial piety governs the realm—it is the highest duty of kings.

sentences.zh: 宜遵聖性以光道訓，既葬之後，素服臨朝。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should follow sacred nature to glorify moral instruction; after burial, attend court in plain garments."
translations.idiomatic: Follow your nature to honor the Way; after burial, hold court in plain dress."

sentences.zh: 尹緯駁曰：「嵩矯常越禮，請付有司論罪。」

translations.literal: Yin Wei rebutted, saying: "Song perverts custom and oversteps ritual—hand him to the authorities for judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei objected that Song violated custom and asked he be punished."

sentences.zh: 興曰：「嵩忠臣孝子，有何罪乎！

translations.literal: Xing said: "Song is a loyal minister and filial son—what crime has he!
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, "Song is loyal and filial—what crime is that!

sentences.zh: 其一如嵩議。」

translations.literal: Let all be as Song proposed."
translations.idiomatic: Do as Song advised."

sentences.zh: 鮮卑薛勃叛秦，秦主興自將討之。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Xue Bo rebelled against Qin; Qin ruler Xing personally led troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei Xue Bo rebelled; Yao Xing marched against him in person.

sentences.zh: 勃敗，奔沒弈干，沒弈干執送之。

translations.literal: Bo was defeated, fled to Moyigan, and Moyigan seized him and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was beaten, fled to Moyigan, who captured and delivered him.

sentences.zh: 秦泫氏男姚買得謀弒秦主興，不克而死。

translations.literal: Yao Maide of Qin Xuan clan plotted to assassinate Qin ruler Xing but failed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Maide of the Xuan clan plotted to kill Yao Xing, failed, and died.

sentences.zh: 秦主興入寇湖城，弘農太守陶仲山、華山太守董邁皆降之。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Xing invaded Hucheng; Hongnong Administrator Tao Zhongshan and Huashan Administrator Dong Mai both surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing invaded Hucheng; Tao Zhongshan of Hongnong and Dong Mai of Huashan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂至陝城，進寇上洛，拔之。

translations.literal: He then reached Shancheng, advanced to raid Shangluo, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Shancheng, raided Shangluo, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 遣姚崇寇洛陽，河南太守夏侯宗之固守金墉，崇攻之不克，乃徙流民二萬餘戶而還。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Chong to raid Luoyang; Henan Administrator Xiahou Zongzhi held firm at Jinyong; Chong could not take it and moved more than twenty thousand displaced people back.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Chong against Luoyang; Xiahou Zongzhi held Jinyong; Chong failed and relocated more than twenty thousand refugees.

sentences.zh: 武都氐屠飛、啖鐵等據方山以叛秦，興遣姚紹等討之，斬飛、鐵。

translations.literal: The Di of Wudu, Tu Fei and Tan Tie, and others held Fangshan and rebelled against Qin; Xing sent Yao Shao and others to attack them and beheaded Fei and Tie.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Fei and Tan Tie of Wudu Di held Fangshan in revolt; Yao Xing sent Yao Shao, who killed them.

sentences.zh: 興勤於政事，延納善言，京兆杜瑾等皆以論事得顯拔，天水姜龕等以儒學見尊禮，給事黃門侍郎古成詵等以文章參機密。

translations.literal: Xing was diligent in government, welcomed good counsel; Du Jin of Jingzhao and others were prominently promoted for policy debate; Jiang Kan of Tianshui and others were honored for Confucian learning; Gu Cheng Shen of the Secretariat and others joined in confidential deliberations for their literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing worked hard at government and welcomed good advice; Du Jin and others rose by policy debate, Jiang Kan by Confucian learning, and Gu Cheng Shen by literary talent in confidential posts.

sentences.zh: 詵剛介雅正，以風教為己任。

translations.literal: Shen was upright, refined, and took moral instruction as his own duty.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng Shen was upright and made moral reform his mission.

sentences.zh: 京兆韋高慕阮籍之為人，居母喪，彈琴餘酒；

translations.literal: Wei Gao of Jingzhao admired Ruan Ji's conduct; during mourning for his mother he still played the zither and drank wine;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao of Jingzhao admired Ruan Ji; in mourning for his mother he still played music and drank;

sentences.zh: 詵聞之而泣，持劍求高，欲殺之，高懼而逃匿。

translations.literal: When Shen heard of it he wept, took a sword and sought Gao, intending to kill him; Gao feared this and fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Shen wept on hearing it, seized a sword to kill Gao, who fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 中山饑甚，慕容麟帥二萬餘人出據新市。

translations.literal: Famine in Zhongshan was extreme; Murong Lin led more than twenty thousand men out to occupy Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Starvation in Zhongshan was severe; Murong Lin led more than twenty thousand out to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 甲子晦，魏王珪進軍攻之。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the last day of the month, Wei King Gui advanced to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the month's last day, Tuoba Gui attacked him.

sentences.zh: 太史令晁崇曰：「不吉。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Chao Chong said: "It is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Astrologer Chao Chong said, "This day is ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 昔紂以甲子亡，謂之疾日，兵家忌之。」

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou of Shang perished on jiazi—it is called an ill day, and military men avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Shang fell on jiazi—the "ill day" armies shun."

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「紂以甲子亡，周武不以甲子興乎？」

translations.literal: Gui said: "Zhou of Shang perished on jiazi—did King Wu of Zhou not rise on jiazi?"
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui said, "Shang fell on jiazi—did King Wu of Zhou not rise on jiazi?"

sentences.zh: 崇無以對。

translations.literal: Chong had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chong could not answer.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙寅，麟退阻泒水。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingyin, Lin withdrew and blocked the Gushui.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingyin, Lin retreated to hold the Gushui.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，珪與麟戰於義台，大破之，斬首九千餘級。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Gui fought Lin at Yitai and inflicted a great defeat, beheading more than nine thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Tuoba Gui routed Murong Lin at Yitai, taking more than nine thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 麟與數十騎馳取妻子入西山，遂奔鄴。

translations.literal: Lin with several dozen horsemen galloped to fetch his wife and children and entered the western hills, then fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Lin fled with a few dozen riders, gathered his family into the western hills, and ran to Ye.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏克中山，燕公卿、尚書、將吏、士卒降者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Wei took Zhongshan; Yan dukes, ministers, Directors of the Imperial Secretariat, officers, and soldiers who surrendered numbered more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Wei captured Zhongshan; more than twenty thousand Yan officials, clerks, and soldiers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 張驤、李沈等先嘗降魏，覆亡去；

translations.literal: Zhang Yang, Li Chen, and others had once surrendered to Wei and then turned back and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang, Li Chen, and others had surrendered to Wei and then rebelled;

sentences.zh: 珪入城，皆赦之。

translations.literal: When Gui entered the city, he pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui pardoned them all on entering the city.

sentences.zh: 得燕璽緩，圖書、府庫珍寶以萬數，班賞群臣將士有差。

translations.literal: He obtained Yan's imperial seal and cord, books, and treasury treasures numbering in the tens of thousands; rewards were distributed in graded shares to ministers, generals, and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yan's seal, archives, and treasures by the myriad and rewarded ministers and soldiers by rank.

sentences.zh: 追謚弟觚為秦愍王。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his younger brother Gu as Prince Min of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his brother Tuoba Gu as Prince Min of Qin.

sentences.zh: 發慕容詳塚，斬其屍；

translations.literal: He opened Murong Xiang's tomb and beheaded the corpse;
translations.idiomatic: He opened Murong Xiang's tomb and beheaded the corpse;

sentences.zh: 收殺觚者高霸、程同，皆夷五族，以大刃剉之。

translations.literal: He seized and executed Gao Ba and Cheng Tong, who had killed Gu, exterminating both clans to the fifth degree and cutting them apart with great blades.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Gao Ba and Cheng Tong, Gu's killers, exterminating their families to the fifth degree and hacking them apart.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，遣三萬騎就衛王儀，將攻鄴。

translations.literal: On dinghai, he sent thirty thousand horsemen to join Prince of Wei Yi and prepare to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, he sent thirty thousand horse to Prince of Wei Tuoba Yi to attack Ye.

sentences.zh: 秦長水校尉姚珍奔西秦，西秦王乾歸以女妻之。

translations.literal: Qin Chief of the Changshui Commandant Yao Zhen fled to Western Qin; Western Qin ruler Qiangui gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Chief of Changshui Yao Zhen fled to Western Qin; Qifu Qiangui gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 河南鮮卑吐秣等十二部大人，皆附於禿髮烏孤。

translations.literal: Twelve tribal chiefs of Henan Xianbei Tumu and others all attached themselves to Tufa Wugu.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve Henan Xianbei chiefs including Tumu submitted to Tufa Wugu.

sentences.zh: 燕人有自中山至龍城者，言拓跋涉珪衰弱，司徒德完守鄴城。

translations.literal: A man of Yan who had come from Zhongshan to Longcheng said Tuoba Gui was weak and that Minister of Works De was holding Ye securely.
translations.idiomatic: A Yan man from Zhongshan told Longcheng that Tuoba Gui was weak and Murong De held Ye firm.

sentences.zh: 會德表至，勸燕主寶南還，寶於是大簡士馬，將復取中原。

translations.literal: When De's memorial arrived urging Yan ruler Bao to return south, Bao thereupon mustered troops and horses on a large scale, intending to recover the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong De's memorial arrived urging Murong Bao south, Bao mustered a great host to recover the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 遣鴻臚魯邃冊拜德為丞相、冀州牧，南夏公候牧守皆聽承製封拜。

translations.literal: He sent Grand Master of the Palace Lu Sui with credentials to appoint De Chancellor and Governor of Jizhou; southern Xia dukes, marquises, and prefects were all allowed to enfeoff and appoint by imperial writ.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lu Sui to appoint De Chancellor and Governor of Jizhou, with southern officials empowered to grant titles.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸丑，燕大赦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guichou, Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guichou, Later Yan declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十二月，調兵悉集，戒嚴在頓，遣將軍啟侖南視形勢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, mobilized troops all assembled; defenses were manned; General Qilun was sent south to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, troops assembled, defenses were set, and General Qilun was sent south to scout.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，慕容麟至鄴，復稱趙王，說范陽王德曰：「魏既克中山，將乘勝攻鄴，鄴中雖有蓄積，然城大難固，且人心恇懼，不可守也。

translations.literal: On yihai, Murong Lin reached Ye, again styled himself Prince of Zhao, and said to the Prince of Fanyang, De: "Wei has taken Zhongshan and will press the victory to attack Ye; though Ye has stores, the city is large and hard to hold, and hearts are fearful—it cannot be defended.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Murong Lin reached Ye, took the title Prince of Zhao again, and told Murong De, "Wei has Zhongshan and will strike Ye; stores are plentiful but the walls are vast, morale is shaken, and the city cannot hold.

sentences.zh: 不如南趣滑台，阻河以待魏，伺釁而動，河北庶可復也。」

translations.literal: Better to hurry south to Huatai, block the river to await Wei, watch for a chance to move, and perhaps recover Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: Better to flee south to Huatai, hold the Yellow River against Wei, and wait for a chance to retake Hebei."

sentences.zh: 時魯陽王和鎮滑台，和，垂之弟子也，亦遣使迎德，德許之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Luyang He was stationed at Huatai; He was a younger son of Chui's younger brother; he also sent envoys to welcome De, and De agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Luyang Murong He held Huatai—Chui's nephew—and also sent for De, who agreed.
